bevy_a11y::AccessibilityRequested.doc: Tracks whether an assistive technology has requested accessibility information.

bevy_a11y::ManageAccessibilityUpdates.doc: Determines whether Bevy's ECS updates the accessibility tree.

bevy_animation::ActiveAnimation.doc: An animation that an `AnimationPlayer` is currently either playing or was playing, but is presently paused.

bevy_animation::AnimatedBy.doc: A component that links an animated entity to an entity containing an `AnimationPlayer`. Typically used alongside the `AnimationTargetId` component - the linked `AnimationPlayer` plays `AnimationClip` assets, and the `AnimationTargetId` identifies which curves in the `AnimationClip` will affect the target entity.

bevy_animation::AnimationTargetId.doc: A component that identifies which parts of an `AnimationClip` asset can be applied to an entity. Typically used alongside the `AnimatedBy` component.

fields.Never: The animation will finish after running once.
fields.Count: The animation will finish after running "n" times.

bevy_animation::graph::AnimationGraphHan.doc: A `Handle` to the `AnimationGraph` to be used by the `AnimationPlayer` on the same entity.

bevy_animation::transition::AnimationTra.doc: An animation that is being faded out as part of a transition
Manages fade-out of animation blend factors, allowing for smooth transitions between animations.

bevy_anti_alias::contrast_adaptive_sharp.doc: Applies a contrast adaptive sharpening (CAS) filter to the camera.

fields.sharpening_strength: Adjusts sharpening strength. Higher values increase the amount of sharpening.
fields.denoise: Whether to try and avoid sharpening areas that are already noisy.

bevy_anti_alias::fxaa::Fxaa.doc: A component for enabling Fast Approximate Anti-Aliasing (FXAA) for a `bevy_camera::Camera`.

fields.edge_threshold: Use lower sensitivity for a sharper, faster, result. Use higher sensitivity for a slower, smoother, result. `Ultra` and `Extreme` settings can result in significant smearing and loss of detail.
fields.edge_threshold_min: Trims the algorithm from processing darks.

bevy_anti_alias::smaa::Smaa.doc: A component for enabling Subpixel Morphological Anti-Aliasing (SMAA) for a `bevy_camera::Camera`.

fields.preset: A predefined set of SMAA parameters: i.e. a quality level.

bevy_anti_alias::smaa::SmaaPreset.doc: A preset quality level for SMAA.

fields.Low: Four search steps; no diagonal or corner detection.
fields.Medium: Eight search steps; no diagonal or corner detection.
fields.High: Sixteen search steps, 8 diagonal search steps, and corner detection.
fields.Ultra: Thirty-two search steps, 8 diagonal search steps, and corner detection.

bevy_anti_alias::taa::TemporalAntiAliasi.doc: Component to apply temporal anti-aliasing to a 3D camera.

fields.reset: Set to true to delete the saved temporal history (past frames).

bevy_app::app::AppExit.doc: A `Message` that indicates the `App` should exit. If one or more of these are present at the end of an update, the runner will end and (maybe) return control to the caller.

fields.Error: The `App` experienced an unhandleable error. Holds the exit code we expect our app to return.

bevy_asset::assets::AssetIndex.doc: A generational runtime-only identifier for a specific `Asset` stored in `Assets`. This is optimized for efficient runtime usage and is not suitable for identifying assets across app runs.

bevy_audio::audio::DefaultSpatialScale.doc: The default scale factor applied to the positions of audio sources and listeners for spatial audio. Can be overridden for individual sounds in `PlaybackSettings`.

bevy_audio::audio::PlaybackMode.doc: The way Bevy manages the sound playback.

fields.Once: Play the sound once. Do nothing when it ends.
fields.Despawn: Despawn the entity and its children when the sound finishes playing.
fields.Remove: Remove the audio components from the entity, when the sound finishes playing.

bevy_audio::audio::PlaybackSettings.doc: Initial settings to be used when audio starts playing.

fields.paused: Create the sink in paused state. Useful for "deferred playback", if you want to prepare the entity, but hear the sound later.
fields.muted: Whether to create the sink in muted state or not.
fields.spatial: Enables spatial audio for this source.
fields.spatial_scale: Optional scale factor applied to the positions of this audio source and the listener, overriding the default value configured on `AudioPlugin::default_spatial_scale`.
fields.start_position: The point in time in the audio clip where playback should start. If set to `None`, it will play from the beginning of the clip.
fields.duration: How long the audio should play before stopping. If set, the clip will play for at most the specified duration. If set to `None`, it will play for as long as it can.

bevy_audio::audio::SpatialListener.doc: Settings for the listener for spatial audio sources.

fields.left_ear_offset: Left ear position relative to the `GlobalTransform`.
fields.right_ear_offset: Right ear position relative to the `GlobalTransform`.

bevy_audio::audio::SpatialScale.doc: A scale factor applied to the positions of audio sources and listeners for spatial audio.

bevy_audio::volume::GlobalVolume.doc: Use this `Resource` to control the global volume of all audio.

fields.volume: The global volume of all audio.

bevy_audio::volume::Volume.doc: A `Volume` represents an audio source's volume level.

fields.Linear: Create a new `Volume` from the given volume in the linear scale.
fields.Decibels: Create a new `Volume` from the given volume in decibels.

bevy_camera::Viewport.doc: Render viewport configuration for the `Camera` component.

fields.physical_position: The physical position to render this viewport to within the `RenderTarget` of this `Camera`. (0,0) corresponds to the top-left corner
fields.physical_size: The physical size of the viewport rectangle to render to within the `RenderTarget` of this `Camera`. The origin of the rectangle is in the top-left corner.
fields.depth: The minimum and maximum depth to render (on a scale from 0.0 to 1.0).

bevy_camera::camera::Camera.doc: The defining `Component` for camera entities, storing information about how and what to render through this camera.

fields.viewport: If set, this camera will render to the given `Viewport` rectangle within the configured `RenderTarget`.
fields.order: Cameras with a higher order are rendered later, and thus on top of lower order cameras.
fields.is_active: If this is set to `true`, this camera will be rendered to its specified `RenderTarget`. If `false`, this camera will not be rendered.
fields.computed: Computed values for this camera, such as the projection matrix and the render target size.
fields.msaa_writeback: Controls when MSAA writeback occurs for this camera. See `MsaaWriteback` for available options.
fields.clear_color: The clear color operation to perform on the render target.
fields.invert_culling: Whether to switch culling mode so that materials that request backface culling cull front faces, and vice versa.
fields.sub_camera_view: If set, this camera will be a sub camera of a large view, defined by a `SubCameraView`.

bevy_camera::camera::CameraMainTextureUs.doc: This component lets you control the `TextureUsages` field of the main texture generated for the camera

bevy_camera::camera::CameraOutputMode.doc: Control how this `Camera` outputs once rendering is completed.

fields.Write: Writes the camera output to configured render target.
fields.Skip: Skips writing the camera output to the configured render target. The output will remain in the Render Target's "intermediate" textures, which a camera with a higher order should write to the render target using `CameraOutputMode::Write`. The "skip" mode can easily prevent render results from being displayed, or cause them to be lost. Only use this if you know what you are doing! In camera setups with multiple active cameras rendering to the same `RenderTarget`, the Skip mode can be used to remove unnecessary / redundant writes to the final output texture, removing unnecessary render passes.

bevy_camera::camera::Exposure.doc: How much energy a `Camera3d` absorbs from incoming light.

bevy_camera::camera::ImageRenderTarget.doc: A render target that renders to an `Image`.

fields.scale_factor: The scale factor of the render target image, corresponding to the scale factor for a window target. This should almost always be 1.0.

bevy_camera::camera::MainPassResolutionO.doc: Override the resolution a 3d camera's main pass is rendered at.

bevy_camera::camera::ManualTextureViewHa.doc: A unique id that corresponds to a specific `ManualTextureView` in the `ManualTextureViews` collection.

bevy_camera::camera::NormalizedRenderTar.doc: Normalized version of the render target.

fields.Window: Window to which the camera's view is rendered.
fields.Image: Image to which the camera's view is rendered.
fields.TextureView: Texture View to which the camera's view is rendered. Useful when the texture view needs to be created outside of Bevy, for example OpenXR.
fields.None: The camera won't render to any color target.

bevy_camera::camera::RenderTarget.doc: The "target" that a `Camera` will render to. For example, this could be a `Window` swapchain or an `Image`.

fields.Window: Window to which the camera's view is rendered.
fields.Image: Image to which the camera's view is rendered.
fields.TextureView: Texture View to which the camera's view is rendered. Useful when the texture view needs to be created outside of Bevy, for example OpenXR.
fields.None: The camera won't render to any color target.

fields.physical_size: The physical size of this render target (in physical pixels, ignoring scale factor).
fields.scale_factor: The scale factor of this render target.

bevy_camera::camera::ShadowLodOrigin.doc: The entity that Bevy uses to resolve visibility ranges when no specific camera is applicable.

bevy_camera::camera::SubCameraView.doc: Settings to define a camera sub view.

fields.full_size: Size of the entire camera view

bevy_camera::camera::Viewport.doc: Render viewport configuration for the `Camera` component.

fields.physical_position: The physical position to render this viewport to within the `RenderTarget` of this `Camera`. (0,0) corresponds to the top-left corner
fields.physical_size: The physical size of the viewport rectangle to render to within the `RenderTarget` of this `Camera`. The origin of the rectangle is in the top-left corner.
fields.depth: The minimum and maximum depth to render (on a scale from 0.0 to 1.0).

bevy_camera::clear_color::ClearColor.doc: A `Resource` that stores the default color that cameras use to clear the screen between frames.

bevy_camera::clear_color::ClearColorConf.doc: For a camera, specifies the color used to clear the viewport before rendering or when writing to the final render target texture.

fields.Default: The clear color is taken from the world's `ClearColor` resource.
fields.Custom: The given clear color is used, overriding the `ClearColor` resource defined in the world.
fields.None: No clear color is used: the camera will simply draw on top of anything already in the viewport.

bevy_camera::clear_color::MsaaWriteback.doc: Controls when MSAA writeback occurs for a camera.

fields.Off: Never perform MSAA writeback for this camera.
fields.Auto: Perform MSAA writeback only when the main pass must load existing content: a fullscreen camera whose main texture a lower camera wrote this frame, or a camera that preserves content across frames with `ClearColorConfig::None`.
fields.Always: Always perform MSAA writeback, even if this is the first camera rendering to the target. This is useful when content has been written directly to the main texture (e.g., via `write_texture`) and needs to be preserved through the MSAA render pass.

bevy_camera::components::Camera2d.doc: A 2D camera component. Enables the 2D render graph for a `Camera`.

bevy_camera::components::Camera3d.doc: A 3D camera component. Enables the main 3D render graph for a `Camera`.

fields.depth_load_op: The depth clear operation to perform for the main 3d pass.
fields.depth_texture_usages: The texture usages for the depth texture created for the main 3d pass.

bevy_camera::components::Camera3dDepthLo.doc: The depth clear operation to perform for the main 3d pass.

fields.Clear: Clear with a specified value. Note that 0.0 is the far plane due to bevy's use of reverse-z projections.

bevy_camera::components::CompositingSpac.doc: Color space for alpha compositing. Affects how overlapping semi-transparent layers blend.

fields.Srgb: Gamma-encoded blending. Matches most image editors. Uses default sRGB target.
fields.Oklab: Perceptually uniform blending. Often smoother gradients. Requires `Hdr` because its value can be outside [0, 1].

bevy_camera::components::Hdr.doc: If this component is added to a camera, the camera will use an intermediate "high dynamic range" render texture. This allows rendering with a wider range of lighting values. However, this does *not* affect whether the camera will render with hdr display output (which bevy does not support currently) and only affects the intermediate render texture.

bevy_camera::primitives::Aabb.doc: An axis-aligned bounding box, defined by: - a center, - the distances from the center to each faces along the axis, the faces are orthogonal to the axis.

bevy_camera::primitives::CubemapLayout.doc: Cubemap layout defines the order of images in a packed cubemap image.

fields.CrossVertical: layout in a vertical cross format ```text +y -x -z +x -y +z ```
fields.CrossHorizontal: layout in a horizontal cross format ```text +y -x -z +x +z -y ```

bevy_camera::primitives::Frustum.doc: A frustum component is used on an entity with a `Camera` component to determine which entities will be considered for rendering by this camera. All entities with an `Aabb` component that are not contained by (or crossing the boundary of) the frustum will not be rendered, and not be used in rendering computations.

bevy_camera::primitives::Sphere.doc: A sphere, defined by a center and a radius.

bevy_camera::projection::CustomProjectio.doc: Holds a dynamic `CameraProjection` trait object. Use `Projection::custom()` to construct a custom projection.

bevy_camera::projection::OrthographicPro.doc: Project a 3D space onto a 2D surface using parallel lines, i.e., unlike `PerspectiveProjection`, the size of objects remains the same regardless of their distance to the camera.

fields.near: The distance of the near clipping plane in world units.
fields.far: The distance of the far clipping plane in world units.
fields.viewport_origin: Specifies the origin of the viewport as a normalized position from 0 to 1, where (0, 0) is the bottom left and (1, 1) is the top right. This determines where the camera's position sits inside the viewport.
fields.scaling_mode: How the projection will scale to the viewport.
fields.area: The area that the projection covers relative to `viewport_origin`.

bevy_camera::projection::PerspectiveProj.doc: A 3D camera projection in which distant objects appear smaller than close objects.

fields.fov: The vertical field of view (FOV) in radians.
fields.aspect_ratio: The aspect ratio (width divided by height) of the viewing frustum.
fields.near: The distance from the camera in world units of the viewing frustum's near plane.
fields.far: The distance from the camera in world units of the viewing frustum's far plane.
fields.near_clip_plane: The orientation of a custom clipping plane, as well as its distance from the camera.

bevy_camera::projection::Projection.doc: Component that defines how to compute a `Camera`'s projection matrix.

fields.Fixed: Manually specify the projection's size, ignoring window resizing. The image will stretch.
fields.AutoMin: Keeping the aspect ratio while the axes can't be smaller than given minimum.
fields.AutoMax: Keeping the aspect ratio while the axes can't be bigger than given maximum.
fields.FixedVertical: Keep the projection's height constant; width will be adjusted to match aspect ratio.
fields.FixedHorizontal: Keep the projection's width constant; height will be adjusted to match aspect ratio.

fields.entities: Map of view entity to the visible entities for each cascade frustum.

bevy_camera::visibility::DynamicSkinnedM.doc: Use this component to enable dynamic skinned mesh bounds. The `Aabb` component of the skinned mesh will be automatically updated each frame based on the current joint transforms.

bevy_camera::visibility::InheritedVisibi.doc: Whether or not an entity is visible in the hierarchy.

bevy_camera::visibility::NoFrustumCullin.doc: Use this component to opt-out of built-in frustum culling for entities, see `Frustum`.

bevy_camera::visibility::ViewVisibility.doc: Algorithmically computed indication of whether an entity is visible and should be extracted for rendering.

bevy_camera::visibility::Visibility.doc: User indication of whether an entity is visible. Propagates down the entity hierarchy.

fields.Inherited: An entity with `Visibility::Inherited` will inherit the Visibility of its `ChildOf` target.
fields.Hidden: An entity with `Visibility::Hidden` will be unconditionally hidden.
fields.Visible: An entity with `Visibility::Visible` will be unconditionally visible.

bevy_camera::visibility::VisibleEntities.doc: Collection of entities visible from the current view.

bevy_camera::visibility::VisibleMeshEnti.doc: Collection of mesh entities visible for 3D lighting.

bevy_camera::visibility::range::Visibili.doc: Specifies the range of distances that this entity must be from the camera in order to be rendered.

fields.start_margin: The range of distances, in world units, between which this entity will smoothly fade into view as the camera zooms out.
fields.end_margin: The range of distances, in world units, between which this entity will smoothly fade out of view as the camera zooms out.
fields.use_aabb: If set to true, Bevy will use the center of the axis-aligned bounding box (`Aabb`) as the position of the mesh for the purposes of visibility range computation.

bevy_camera::visibility::render_layers::.doc: Defines which rendering layers an entity belongs to.

fields.Srgba: A color in the sRGB color space with alpha.
fields.LinearRgba: A color in the linear sRGB color space with alpha.

bevy_core_pipeline::prepass::DeferredPre.doc: If added to a `bevy_camera::Camera3d` then deferred materials will be rendered to the deferred gbuffer texture and will be available to subsequent passes. Note the default deferred lighting plugin also requires `DepthPrepass` to work correctly.

bevy_core_pipeline::prepass::DepthPrepas.doc: If added to a `bevy_camera::Camera3d` then depth values will be copied to a separate texture available to the main pass.

bevy_core_pipeline::prepass::MotionVecto.doc: If added to a `bevy_camera::Camera3d` then screen space motion vectors will be copied to a separate texture available to the main pass.

bevy_core_pipeline::prepass::NormalPrepa.doc: If added to a `bevy_camera::Camera3d` then vertex world normals will be copied to a separate texture available to the main pass. Normals will have normal map textures already applied.

bevy_core_pipeline::prepass::background_.doc: When added to a camera with `MotionVectorPrepass`, disables the automatic background motion vector prepass.

bevy_core_pipeline::schedule::RootNonCam.doc: A render-world marker component for a view that corresponds to neither a camera nor a camera-associated shadow map.

fields.QuadraticInOut: Behaves as `EaseFunction::QuadraticIn` for t < 0.5 and as `EaseFunction::QuadraticOut` for t >= 0.5
fields.CubicInOut: Behaves as `EaseFunction::CubicIn` for t < 0.5 and as `EaseFunction::CubicOut` for t >= 0.5
fields.QuarticInOut: Behaves as `EaseFunction::QuarticIn` for t < 0.5 and as `EaseFunction::QuarticOut` for t >= 0.5
fields.QuinticInOut: Behaves as `EaseFunction::QuinticIn` for t < 0.5 and as `EaseFunction::QuinticOut` for t >= 0.5
fields.SmoothStepIn: Behaves as the first half of `EaseFunction::SmoothStep`.
fields.SmoothStepOut: Behaves as the second half of `EaseFunction::SmoothStep`.
fields.SmootherStepIn: Behaves as the first half of `EaseFunction::SmootherStep`.
fields.SmootherStepOut: Behaves as the second half of `EaseFunction::SmootherStep`.

fields.CircularInOut: Behaves as `EaseFunction::CircularIn` for t < 0.5 and as `EaseFunction::CircularOut` for t >= 0.5

fields.ElasticInOut: Behaves as `EaseFunction::ElasticIn` for t < 0.5 and as `EaseFunction::ElasticOut` for t >= 0.5
fields.BackInOut: Behaves as `EaseFunction::BackIn` for t < 0.5 and as `EaseFunction::BackOut` for t >= 0.5
fields.BounceInOut: Behaves as `EaseFunction::BounceIn` for t < 0.5 and as `EaseFunction::BounceOut` for t >= 0.5

bevy_curve::easing::JumpAt.doc: Configuration options for the `EaseFunction::Steps` curves. This closely replicates the [CSS step function specification].

fields.End: Indicates that the last step happens when the animation ends.

fields.Both: Indicates both early and late jumps happen.

bevy_ecs::observer::distributed_storage:.doc: Tracks a list of entity observers for the `Entity` `ObservedBy` is added to.

bevy_ecs::resource::IsResource.doc: A marker component for entities that have a Resource component.

fields.None: The center of the bottom-left tile
fields.Center: The center of the bottom-left tile

bevy_ecs_tilemap::map::HexCoordSystem.doc: Different hex grid coordinate systems. You can find out more at this link: <https://www.redblobgames.com/grids/hexagons/>

bevy_ecs_tilemap::map::TilemapGridSize.doc: Size of the tiles on the grid in pixels. This can be used to overlay tiles on top of each other. Ex. A 16x16 pixel tile can be overlapped by 8 pixels by using a grid size of 16x8.

bevy_ecs_tilemap::map::TilemapId.doc: A component which stores a reference to the tilemap entity.

bevy_ecs_tilemap::map::TilemapSize.doc: Size of the tilemap in tiles.

bevy_ecs_tilemap::map::TilemapTextureSiz.doc: Size of the atlas texture in pixels.

bevy_ecs_tilemap::map::TilemapTileSize.doc: Size of the tiles in pixels

fields.Isometric: Used to change the rendering mode to Isometric.

bevy_ecs_tilemap::tiles::TileColor.doc: A custom color for the tile.

bevy_ecs_tilemap::tiles::TilePos.doc: A tile position in the tilemap grid.

bevy_feathers::controls::ButtonVariant.doc: Color variants for buttons. This also functions as a component used by the dynamic styling system to identify which entities are buttons.

fields.Primary: A button with a more prominent color, this is used for "call to action" buttons, default buttons for dialog boxes, and so on.

fields.Character: A key string that corresponds to the character typed by the user, taking into account the user’s current locale setting, and any system-level keyboard mapping overrides that are in effect.
fields.Unidentified: This variant is used when the key cannot be translated to any other variant.
fields.Dead: Contains the text representation of the dead-key when available.
fields.Fn: The Function switch `Fn` key. Activating this key simultaneously with another key changes that key’s value to an alternate character or function. This key is often handled directly in the keyboard hardware and does not usually generate key events.
fields.FnLock: The Function-Lock (`FnLock` or `F-Lock`) key. Activating this key switches the mode of the keyboard to changes some keys' values to an alternate character or function. This key is often handled directly in the keyboard hardware and does not usually generate key events.
fields.NumLock: The `NumLock` or Number Lock key. Used to toggle numpad mode function for interpreting subsequent keyboard input.
fields.ScrollLock: Toggle between scrolling and cursor movement modes.
fields.Shift: Used to enable shift modifier function for interpreting concurrent or subsequent keyboard input.
fields.Symbol: The Symbol modifier key (used on some virtual keyboards).
fields.SymbolLock: The SymbolLock key, only on web.
fields.Meta: Legacy modifier key. Also called "Super" in certain places.
fields.Super: Used to enable "super" modifier function for interpreting concurrent or subsequent keyboard input. This key value is used for the "Windows Logo" key and the Apple `Command` or `⌘` key.
fields.Enter: The `Enter` or `↵` key. Used to activate current selection or accept current input. This key value is also used for the `Return` (Macintosh numpad) key. This key value is also used for the Android `KEYCODE_DPAD_CENTER`.
fields.Space: Used in text to insert a space between words. Usually located below the character keys.
fields.End: The End key, used with keyboard entry to go to the end of content (`KEYCODE_MOVE_END`).
fields.Home: The Home key, used with keyboard entry, to go to start of content (`KEYCODE_MOVE_HOME`). For the mobile phone `Home` key (which goes to the phone’s main screen), use `GoHome`.
fields.PageDown: Scroll down or display next page of content.
fields.PageUp: Scroll up or display previous page of content.
fields.Backspace: Used to remove the character to the left of the cursor. This key value is also used for the key labeled `Delete` on macOS keyboards.
fields.Delete: Used to delete the character to the right of the cursor. This key value is also used for the key labeled `Delete` on macOS keyboards when `Fn` is active.
fields.EraseEof: The Erase to End of Field key. This key deletes all characters from the current cursor position to the end of the current field.
fields.Insert: Toggle between text modes for insertion or overtyping. (`KEYCODE_INSERT`)
fields.Accept: The Accept (Commit, OK) key. Accept current option or input method sequence conversion.
fields.Cancel: The Cancel key. (on linux and web)
fields.ContextMenu: Show the application’s context menu. This key is commonly found between the right `Super` key and the right `Control` key.
fields.Escape: The `Esc` key. This key was originally used to initiate an escape sequence, but is now more generally used to exit or "escape" the current context, such as closing a dialog or exiting full screen mode.

fields.focused_entity: The entity that has acquired focus.

bevy_input_focus::InputFocus.doc: Resource representing which entity has input focus, if any. Input events (other than pointer-like inputs) will be dispatched to the current focus entity, or to the primary window if no entity has focus.

bevy_input_focus::InputFocusVisible.doc: Resource representing whether the input focus indicator should be visible on UI elements.

bevy_input_focus::autofocus::AutoFocus.doc: Indicates that this widget should automatically receive `InputFocus`.

bevy_input_focus::directional_navigation.doc: Configuration resource for automatic directional navigation and for generating manual navigation edges via `auto_generate_navigation_edges`

fields.min_alignment_factor: Minimum overlap ratio (0.0-1.0) required along the perpendicular axis for cardinal directions.
fields.max_search_distance: Maximum search distance in logical pixels.
fields.prefer_aligned: Whether to prefer nodes that are more aligned with the exact direction.

bevy_input_focus::directional_navigation.doc: A resource that stores the manually specified traversable graph of focusable entities.

fields.neighbors: A directed graph of focusable entities.

bevy_input_focus::directional_navigation.doc: Represents what's near a focusable entity.

fields.Set: The neighbor is known and set.

bevy_input_focus::directional_navigation.doc: The up-to-eight neighbors of a focusable entity, one for each `CompassOctant`.

fields.neighbors: The array of neighbors, one for each `CompassOctant`. The mapping between array elements and directions is determined by `CompassOctant::to_index`.

fields.Navigated: The input was navigated into by the keyboard, gamepad, or default behavior when unknown.
fields.Pressed: The input was pressed into with the mouse or touchpad
fields.Auto: Focus was assigned automatically when an `AutoFocus` component was added.

bevy_input_focus::gained_and_lost::Focus.doc: An `EntityEvent` that is sent when an entity gains `InputFocus`.
An `EntityEvent` that is sent when an entity loses `InputFocus`.

bevy_input_focus::tab_navigation::NavAct.doc: A navigation action that users might take to navigate your user interface in a cyclic fashion.

fields.Next: Navigate to the next focusable entity, wrapping around to the beginning if at the end.
fields.Previous: Navigate to the previous focusable entity, wrapping around to the end if at the beginning.
fields.First: Navigate to the first focusable entity.
fields.Last: Navigate to the last focusable entity.

bevy_input_focus::tab_navigation::TabGro.doc: A component used to mark a tree of entities as containing tabbable elements.

fields.order: The order of the tab group relative to other tab groups.
fields.modal: Whether this is a 'modal' group. If true, then tabbing within the group (that is, if the current focus entity is a child of this group) will cycle through the children of this group. If false, then tabbing within the group will cycle through all non-modal tab groups.

bevy_input_focus::tab_navigation::TabInd.doc: A component which indicates that an entity wants to participate in tab navigation.

bevy_light::NotShadowCaster.doc: Add this component to make a `Mesh3d` not cast shadows.

bevy_light::NotShadowReceiver.doc: Add this component to make a `Mesh3d` not receive shadows.

bevy_light::ShadowFilteringMethod.doc: Add this component to a `Camera3d` to control how to anti-alias shadow edges.

fields.Gaussian: Approximates a fixed Gaussian blur, good when TAA isn't in use.
fields.Temporal: A randomized filter that varies over time, good when TAA is in use.

bevy_light::TransmittedShadowReceiver.doc: Add this component to make a `Mesh3d` using a PBR material with `StandardMaterial::diffuse_transmission > 0.0` receive shadows on its diffuse transmission lobe. (i.e. its “backside”)

bevy_light::ambient_light::AmbientLight.doc: An ambient light, which lights the entire scene equally.

fields.color: The color of the ambient light.
fields.brightness: A direct scale factor multiplied with `color` before being passed to the shader.
fields.affects_lightmapped_meshes: Whether this ambient light has an effect on meshes with lightmaps.

bevy_light::ambient_light::GlobalAmbient.doc: The global ambient light, which lights the entire scene equally.

fields.color: The color of the ambient light.
fields.brightness: A direct scale factor multiplied with `color` before being passed to the shader.
fields.affects_lightmapped_meshes: Whether this ambient light has an effect on meshes with lightmaps.

bevy_light::cascade::Cascade.doc: A single cascade of a view's shadow map cascade. Several of these are used to cover most of the view to ensure most geometry gets shadows, with some overlap for blending at cascade transitions. Farther away cascades are larger and have a lower effective shadowmap texel per world unit resolution. All cascades have the same pixel dimensions however.

fields.world_from_cascade: The transform of the light, i.e. the view to world matrix.
fields.clip_from_cascade: The orthographic projection for this cascade.
fields.clip_from_world: The view-projection matrix for this cascade, converting world space into light clip space. Importantly, this is derived and stored separately from `view_transform` and `projection` to ensure shadow stability.
fields.texel_size: Size of each shadow map texel in world units.

bevy_light::cascade::CascadeShadowConfig.doc: Controls how cascaded shadow mapping works. Prefer using `CascadeShadowConfigBuilder` to construct an instance.

fields.bounds: The (positive) distance to the far boundary of each cascade.
fields.overlap_proportion: The proportion of overlap each cascade has with the previous cascade.
fields.minimum_distance: The (positive) distance to the near boundary of the first cascade.

fields.cascades: Map from a view to the configuration of each of its `Cascade`s.

bevy_light::cluster::ClusterConfig.doc: Configuration of the clustering strategy for clustered forward rendering

fields.None: Disable cluster calculations for this view
fields.Single: One single cluster. Optimal for low-light complexity scenes or scenes where most lights affect the entire scene.
fields.XYZ: Explicit `X`, `Y` and `Z` counts (may yield non-square `X/Y` clusters depending on the aspect ratio)
fields.FixedZ: Fixed number of `Z` slices, `X` and `Y` calculated to give square clusters with at most total clusters. For top-down games where lights will generally always be within a short depth range, it may be useful to use this configuration with 1 or few `Z` slices. This would reduce the number of lights per cluster by distributing more clusters in screen space `X/Y` which matches how lights are distributed in the scene.

bevy_light::cluster::ClusterFarZMode.doc: Configure the far z-plane mode used for the furthest depth slice for clustered forward rendering

fields.MaxClusterableObjectRange: Calculate the required maximum z-depth based on the clusterable objects that were visible on the previous frame. Makes better use of available clusters, speeding up GPU lighting operations at the expense of using more indices in the clusterable object index lists.

bevy_light::cluster::ClusterZConfig.doc: Configure the depth-slicing strategy for clustered forward rendering

fields.first_slice_depth: Far `Z` plane of the first depth slice
fields.far_z_mode: Strategy for how to evaluate the far `Z` plane of the furthest depth slice

bevy_light::cluster::ClusteredDecal.doc: An object that projects a decal onto surfaces within its bounds.

fields.base_color_texture: The image that the clustered decal projects onto the base color of the surface material.
fields.normal_map_texture: The normal map that the clustered decal projects onto surfaces.
fields.metallic_roughness_texture: The metallic-roughness map that the clustered decal projects onto surfaces.
fields.emissive_texture: The emissive map that the clustered decal projects onto surfaces.
fields.tag: An application-specific tag you can use for any purpose you want, in conjunction with a custom shader.

fields.illuminance: Illuminance in lux (lumens per square meter), representing the amount of light projected onto surfaces by this light source. Lux is used here instead of lumens because a directional light illuminates all surfaces more-or-less the same way (depending on the angle of incidence). Lumens can only be specified for light sources which emit light from a specific area. The default is `light_consts::lux::AMBIENT_DAYLIGHT` = 10,000.
fields.contact_shadows_enabled: Whether this light casts contact shadows.
fields.soft_shadow_size: Whether soft shadows are enabled, and if so, the size of the light.
fields.affects_lightmapped_mesh_diffuse: Whether this directional light contributes diffuse lighting to meshes with lightmaps.
fields.shadow_depth_bias: A value that adjusts the tradeoff between self-shadowing artifacts and proximity of shadows to their casters.
fields.shadow_normal_bias: A bias applied along the direction of the fragment's surface normal. It is scaled to the shadow map's texel size so that it is automatically adjusted to the orthographic projection.

bevy_light::directional_light::Direction.doc: Controls the resolution of `DirectionalLight` and `SpotLight` shadow maps.

fields.size: Must be a power of two to avoid unstable cascade positioning.

bevy_light::directional_light::Direction.doc: Add to a `DirectionalLight` to add a light texture effect. A texture mask is applied to the light source to modulate its intensity, simulating patterns like window shadows, gobo/cookie effects, or soft falloffs.

fields.image: The texture image. Only the R channel is read.
fields.tiled: Whether to tile the image infinitely, or use only a single tile centered at the light's translation

bevy_light::gizmos::LightGizmoColor.doc: Configures how a color is attributed to a light gizmo.

fields.Varied: Random color derived from the light's `Entity`.
fields.MatchLightColor: Take the color of the represented light.
fields.ByLightType: Take the color provided by `LightGizmoConfigGroup` depending on the light kind.

bevy_light::gizmos::ShowLightGizmo.doc: Add this `Component` to an entity to draw any of its lights components (`PointLight`, `SpotLight`, `DirectionalLight` and `RectLight`).

fields.color: Default color strategy for this light gizmo. If `None`, use the one provided by `LightGizmoConfigGroup`.

bevy_light::point_light::PointLight.doc: A light that emits light in all directions from a central point.

fields.color: The color of this light source.
fields.intensity: Luminous power in lumens, representing the amount of light emitted by this source in all directions.
fields.range: Cut-off for the light's area-of-effect. Fragments outside this range will not be affected by this light at all, so it's important to tune this together with `intensity` to prevent hard lighting cut-offs.
fields.radius: Simulates a light source coming from a spherical volume with the given radius.
fields.contact_shadows_enabled: Whether this light casts contact shadows.
fields.affects_lightmapped_mesh_diffuse: Whether this point light contributes diffuse lighting to meshes with lightmaps.
fields.shadow_depth_bias: A bias used when sampling shadow maps to avoid "shadow-acne", or false shadow occlusions that happen as a result of shadow-map fragments not mapping 1:1 to screen-space fragments. Too high of a depth bias can lead to shadows detaching from their casters, or "peter-panning". This bias can be tuned together with `shadow_normal_bias` to correct shadow artifacts for a given scene.
fields.shadow_normal_bias: A bias applied along the direction of the fragment's surface normal. It is scaled to the shadow map's texel size so that it can be small close to the camera and gets larger further away.
fields.shadow_map_near_z: The distance from the light to near Z plane in the shadow map.

bevy_light::point_light::PointLightShado.doc: Controls the resolution of `PointLight` shadow maps.

fields.size: The width and height of each of the 6 faces of the cubemap.

bevy_light::point_light::PointLightTextu.doc: Add to a `PointLight` to add a light texture effect. A texture mask is applied to the light source to modulate its intensity, simulating patterns like window shadows, gobo/cookie effects, or soft falloffs.

fields.image: The texture image. Only the R channel is read.
fields.cubemap_layout: The cubemap layout. The image should be a packed cubemap in one of the formats described by the `CubemapLayout` enum.

bevy_light::probe::EnvironmentMapLight.doc: A pair of cubemap textures that represent the surroundings of a specific area in space.

fields.diffuse_map: The blurry image that represents diffuse radiance surrounding a region.
fields.specular_map: The typically-sharper, mipmapped image that represents specular radiance surrounding a region.
fields.intensity: Scale factor applied to the diffuse and specular light generated by this component.
fields.rotation: World space rotation applied to the environment light cubemaps. This is useful for users who require a different axis, such as the Z-axis, to serve as the vertical axis.
fields.affects_lightmapped_mesh_diffuse: Whether the light from this environment map contributes diffuse lighting to meshes with lightmaps.

bevy_light::probe::GeneratedEnvironmentM.doc: A generated environment map that is filtered at runtime.

fields.environment_map: Source cubemap to be filtered on the GPU, size must be a power of two.
fields.intensity: Scale factor applied to the diffuse and specular light generated by this component. Expressed in cd/m² (candela per square meter).
fields.rotation: World-space rotation applied to the cubemap.
fields.affects_lightmapped_mesh_diffuse: Whether this light contributes diffuse lighting to meshes that already have baked lightmaps.

bevy_light::probe::IrradianceVolume.doc: The component that defines an irradiance volume.

fields.voxels: The 3D texture that represents the ambient cubes, encoded in the format described in `bevy_pbr::light_probe::irradiance_volume`.
fields.intensity: Scale factor applied to the diffuse and specular light generated by this component.
fields.affects_lightmapped_meshes: Whether the light from this irradiance volume has an effect on meshes with lightmaps.

bevy_light::probe::LightProbe.doc: A marker component for a light probe, which is a cuboid region that provides global illumination to all fragments inside it.

fields.falloff: The distance over which the effect of the light probe becomes weaker, on each axis.

bevy_light::probe::ParallaxCorrection.doc: Add this component to a reflection probe to customize *parallax correction*.

fields.Auto: The parallax correction boundaries correspond with the boundaries of the light probe.
fields.Custom: The parallax correction boundaries are specified manually.

bevy_light::probe::Skybox.doc: Adds a skybox to a 3D camera, based on a cubemap texture.

fields.brightness: Scale factor applied to the skybox image. After applying this multiplier to the image samples, the resulting values should be in units of cd/m^2.
fields.rotation: View space rotation applied to the skybox cubemap. This is useful for users who require a different axis, such as the Z-axis, to serve as the vertical axis.

fields.intensity: Luminous power in lumens, representing the amount of light emitted by this source in all directions.
fields.range: Cut-off for the light's area-of-effect. Fragments outside this range will not be affected by this light at all, so it's important to tune this together with `intensity` to prevent hard lighting cut-offs.
fields.width: Width of the light rectangle (along local X).
fields.height: Height of the light rectangle (along local Y).

bevy_light::spot_light::SpotLight.doc: A light that emits light in a given direction from a central point.

fields.intensity: Luminous power in lumens, representing the amount of light emitted by this source in all directions.
fields.range: Range in meters that this light illuminates.
fields.radius: Simulates a light source coming from a spherical volume with the given radius.
fields.contact_shadows_enabled: Whether this light casts contact shadows. Cameras must also have the `ContactShadows` component.
fields.affects_lightmapped_mesh_diffuse: Whether this spot light contributes diffuse lighting to meshes with lightmaps.
fields.shadow_depth_bias: A value that adjusts the tradeoff between self-shadowing artifacts and proximity of shadows to their casters.
fields.shadow_normal_bias: A bias applied along the direction of the fragment's surface normal. It is scaled to the shadow map's texel size so that it can be small close to the camera and gets larger further away.
fields.shadow_map_near_z: The distance from the light to the near Z plane in the shadow map.
fields.outer_angle: Angle defining the distance from the spot light direction to the outer limit of the light's cone of effect. `outer_angle` must be < `PI / 2.0`.
fields.inner_angle: Angle defining the distance from the spot light direction to the inner limit of the light's cone of effect. Light is attenuated from `inner_angle` to `outer_angle` to give a smooth falloff. `inner_angle` should be <= `outer_angle`

bevy_light::spot_light::SpotLightTexture.doc: Add to a `SpotLight` to add a light texture effect. A texture mask is applied to the light source to modulate its intensity, simulating patterns like window shadows, gobo/cookie effects, or soft falloffs.

fields.image: The texture image. Only the R channel is read. Note the border of the image should be entirely black to avoid leaking light.

bevy_light::volumetric::FogVolume.doc: A unit cube of fog at the origin. Can be positioned and scaled with a `Transform`. Only visible by cameras with a `VolumetricFog` component when lit by a directional light with `VolumetricLight`.

fields.density_factor: The density of fog, which measures how dark the fog is.
fields.density_texture: Optional 3D voxel density texture for the fog.
fields.density_texture_offset: Configurable offset of the density texture in UVW coordinates.
fields.absorption: The absorption coefficient, which measures what fraction of light is absorbed by the fog at each step.
fields.scattering: The scattering coefficient, which measures the fraction of light that's scattered toward, and away from, the viewer.
fields.scattering_asymmetry: Measures the fraction of light that's scattered *toward* the camera, as opposed to *away* from the camera.
fields.light_tint: Applies a nonphysical color to the light.
fields.light_intensity: Scales the light by a fixed fraction.

bevy_light::volumetric::VolumetricFog.doc: When placed on a `bevy_camera::Camera3d`, enables volumetric fog and volumetric lighting, also known as light shafts or god rays.

fields.ambient_intensity: The brightness of the ambient light.
fields.jitter: The maximum distance to offset the ray origin randomly by, in meters.
fields.step_count: The number of raymarching steps to perform.

bevy_light::volumetric::VolumetricLight.doc: Add this component to a `DirectionalLight` with a shadow map (`shadow_maps_enabled: true`) to make volumetric fog interact with it.

bevy_material::alpha::AlphaMode.doc: Sets how a material's base color alpha channel is used for transparency.

fields.Opaque: Base color alpha values are overridden to be fully opaque (1.0).
fields.Mask: Reduce transparency to fully opaque or fully transparent based on a threshold.
fields.Blend: The base color alpha value defines the opacity of the color. Standard alpha-blending is used to blend the fragment's color with the color behind it.
fields.Premultiplied: Similar to `AlphaMode::Blend`, however assumes RGB channel values are premultiplied.
fields.AlphaToCoverage: Spreads the fragment out over a hardware-dependent number of sample locations proportional to the alpha value. This requires multisample antialiasing; if MSAA isn't on, this is identical to `AlphaMode::Mask` with a value of 0.5.
fields.Add: Combines the color of the fragments with the colors behind them in an additive process, (i.e. like light) producing lighter results.
fields.Multiply: Combines the color of the fragments with the colors behind them in a multiplicative process, (i.e. like pigments) producing darker results.

bevy_material::opaque::OpaqueRendererMet.doc: Render method used for opaque materials.

fields.cos: The cosine of the rotation angle.
fields.sin: The sine of the rotation angle.

bevy_math::compass::CompassOctant.doc: A compass enum with 8 directions. ```text N (North) ▲ NW   │   NE ╲ │ ╱ W (West) ┼─────► E (East) ╱ │ ╲ SW   │   SE ▼ S (South) ```

bevy_math::direction::Dir2.doc: A normalized vector pointing in a direction in 2D space

bevy_math::direction::Dir3.doc: A normalized vector pointing in a direction in 3D space

bevy_math::rects::rect::Rect.doc: A rectangle defined by two opposite corners.

fields.min: The minimum corner point of the rect.
fields.max: The maximum corner point of the rect.

bevy_math::rects::urect::URect.doc: A rectangle defined by two opposite corners.

fields.min: The minimum corner point of the rect.
fields.max: The maximum corner point of the rect.

fields.cos: The cosine of the rotation angle.
fields.sin: The sine of the rotation angle.

fields.name: The friendly name of the vertex attribute
fields.id: The _unique_ id of the vertex attribute. This will also determine sort ordering when generating vertex buffers. Built-in / standard attributes will use "close to zero" indices. When in doubt, use a random / very large u64 to avoid conflicts.
fields.format: The format of the vertex attribute.

bevy_mesh::components::Mesh2d.doc: A component for 2D meshes. Requires a `MeshMaterial2d` to be rendered, commonly using a `ColorMaterial`.

bevy_mesh::components::Mesh3d.doc: A component for 3D meshes. Requires a `MeshMaterial3d` to be rendered, commonly using a `StandardMaterial`.

bevy_mesh::components::MeshTag.doc: A component that stores an arbitrary index used to identify the mesh instance when rendering.

fields.value: The value made available to the shader.

bevy_mesh::mesh::Mesh.doc: A 3D object made out of vertices representing triangles, lines, or points, with "attribute" values for each vertex.

fields.asset_usage: `std::collections::BTreeMap` with all defined vertex attributes (Positions, Normals, ...) for this mesh. Attribute ids to attribute values. Uses a `BTreeMap` because, unlike `HashMap`, it has a defined iteration order, which allows easy stable `VertexBuffers` (i.e. same buffer order)
fields.enable_raytracing: Whether or not to build a BLAS for use with `bevy_solari` raytracing.
fields.final_aabb: Precomputed min and max extents of the mesh position data. Used mainly for constructing `Aabb`s for frustum culling and decompressing vertex positions. This data will be set if/when a mesh is extracted to the GPU or when compressing positions.
fields.final_uv_ranges: Precomputed min and max extents of the mesh UV channels data. Used mainly for decompressing vertex UVs. This will be set when compressing UVs.

bevy_mesh::morph::MeshMorphWeights.doc: A component that controls the [morph targets] of a mesh. Must be assigned to an entity with a `Mesh3d` component.

fields.Reference: A reference to an entity containing a `MorphWeights` component. This allows a single `MorphWeights` component to control the morph targets of multiple meshes.

bevy_mesh::morph::MorphWeights.doc: Controls the [morph targets] for all child `Mesh3d` entities. In most cases, `MorphWeights` should be considered the "source of truth" when writing [morph targets] for meshes. However you can choose to write child `MeshMorphWeights` if your situation requires more granularity. Just note that if you set `MorphWeights`, it will overwrite child `MeshMorphWeights` values.

bevy_pbr::contact_shadows::ContactShadow.doc: Add this component to a camera to enable contact shadows.

fields.linear_steps: The number of steps to be taken at regular intervals to find an initial intersection.
fields.thickness: When marching the depth buffer, we only have 2.5D information and don't know how thick surfaces are. We shall assume that the depth buffer fragments are cuboids with a constant thickness defined by this parameter.
fields.length: The length of the contact shadow ray in world space.

bevy_pbr::fog::DistanceFog.doc: Configures the “classic” computer graphics distance fog effect, in which objects appear progressively more covered in atmospheric haze the further away they are from the camera. Affects meshes rendered via the PBR `StandardMaterial`.

fields.color: The color of the fog effect.
fields.directional_light_color: Color used to modulate the influence of directional light colors on the fog, where the view direction aligns with each directional light direction, producing a “glow” or light dispersion effect. (e.g. around the sun)
fields.directional_light_exponent: The exponent applied to the directional light alignment calculation. A higher value means a more concentrated “glow”.
fields.falloff: Determines which falloff mode to use, and its parameters.

bevy_pbr::fog::FogFalloff.doc: Allows switching between different fog falloff modes, and configuring their parameters.

fields.Linear: A linear fog falloff that grows in intensity between `start` and `end` distances.
fields.Exponential: An exponential fog falloff with a given `density`.
fields.ExponentialSquared: A squared exponential fog falloff with a given `density`.
fields.Atmospheric: A more general form of the `FogFalloff::Exponential` mode. The falloff formula is separated into two terms, `extinction` and `inscattering`, for a somewhat simplified atmospheric scattering model. Additionally, individual color channels can have their own density values, resulting in a total of six different configuration parameters.

bevy_pbr::lightmap::Lightmap.doc: A component that applies baked indirect diffuse global illumination from a lightmap.

fields.uv_rect: The rectangle within the lightmap texture that the UVs are relative to.
fields.bicubic_sampling: Whether bicubic sampling should be used for sampling this lightmap.

bevy_pbr::material::DefaultOpaqueRendere.doc: Default render method used for opaque materials.

bevy_pbr::pbr_material::StandardMaterial.doc: A material with "standard" properties used in PBR lighting. Standard property values with pictures here: <https://google.github.io/filament/notes/material_properties.html>.

fields.base_color: The color of the surface of the material before lighting.
fields.base_color_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::base_color_texture`.
fields.base_color_texture: The texture component of the material's color before lighting. The actual pre-lighting color is `base_color * this_texture`.
fields.emissive: Color the material "emits" to the camera.
fields.emissive_exposure_weight: The weight in which the camera exposure influences the emissive color. A value of `0.0` means the emissive color is not affected by the camera exposure. In opposition, a value of `1.0` means the emissive color is multiplied by the camera exposure.
fields.emissive_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::emissive_texture`.
fields.emissive_texture: The emissive map, multiplies pixels with `emissive` to get the final "emitting" color of a surface.
fields.metallic_roughness_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::metallic_roughness_texture`.
fields.metallic_roughness_texture: Metallic and roughness maps, stored as a single texture.
fields.reflectance: Specular intensity for non-metals on a linear scale of `[0.0, 1.0]`.
fields.specular_tint: A color with which to modulate the `StandardMaterial::reflectance` for non-metals.
fields.diffuse_transmission: The amount of light transmitted _diffusely_ through the material (i.e. “translucency”).
fields.diffuse_transmission_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::diffuse_transmission_texture`.
fields.diffuse_transmission_texture: A map that modulates diffuse transmission via its alpha channel. Multiplied by `StandardMaterial::diffuse_transmission` to obtain the final result.
fields.specular_transmission: The amount of light transmitted _specularly_ through the material (i.e. via refraction).
fields.specular_transmission_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::specular_transmission_texture`.
fields.specular_transmission_texture: A map that modulates specular transmission via its red channel. Multiplied by `StandardMaterial::specular_transmission` to obtain the final result.
fields.thickness: Thickness of the volume beneath the material surface.
fields.thickness_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::thickness_texture`.
fields.thickness_texture: A map that modulates thickness via its green channel. Multiplied by `StandardMaterial::thickness` to obtain the final result.
fields.ior: The index of refraction of the material.
fields.attenuation_distance: How far, on average, light travels through the volume beneath the material's surface before being absorbed.
fields.attenuation_color: The resulting (non-absorbed) color after white light travels through the attenuation distance.
fields.normal_map_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::normal_map_texture`.
fields.normal_map_texture: Used to fake the lighting of bumps and dents on a material.
fields.flip_normal_map_y: Normal map textures authored for DirectX have their y-component flipped. Set this to flip it to right-handed conventions.
fields.occlusion_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::occlusion_texture`.
fields.occlusion_texture: Specifies the level of exposure to ambient light.
fields.specular_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::specular_texture`.
fields.specular_texture: A map that specifies reflectance for non-metallic materials.
fields.specular_tint_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::specular_tint_texture`.
fields.specular_tint_texture: A map that specifies color adjustment to be applied to the specular reflection for non-metallic materials.
fields.clearcoat: An extra thin translucent layer on top of the main PBR layer. This is typically used for painted surfaces.
fields.clearcoat_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::clearcoat_texture`.
fields.clearcoat_texture: An image texture that specifies the strength of the clearcoat layer in the red channel. Values sampled from this texture are multiplied by the main `StandardMaterial::clearcoat` factor.
fields.clearcoat_perceptual_roughness: The roughness of the clearcoat material. This is specified in exactly the same way as the `StandardMaterial::perceptual_roughness`.
fields.clearcoat_roughness_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::clearcoat_roughness_texture`.
fields.clearcoat_roughness_texture: An image texture that specifies the roughness of the clearcoat level in the green channel. Values from this texture are multiplied by the main `StandardMaterial::clearcoat_perceptual_roughness` factor.
fields.clearcoat_normal_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::clearcoat_normal_texture`.
fields.clearcoat_normal_texture: An image texture that specifies a normal map that is to be applied to the clearcoat layer. This can be used to simulate, for example, scratches on an outer layer of varnish. Normal maps are in the same format as `StandardMaterial::normal_map_texture`.
fields.anisotropy_strength: Increases the roughness along a specific direction, so that the specular highlight will be stretched instead of being a circular lobe.
fields.anisotropy_rotation: The direction of increased roughness, in radians relative to the mesh tangent.
fields.anisotropy_channel: The UV channel to use for the `StandardMaterial::anisotropy_texture`.
fields.anisotropy_texture: An image texture that allows the `StandardMaterial::anisotropy_strength` and `StandardMaterial::anisotropy_rotation` to vary across the mesh.
fields.double_sided: Support two-sided lighting by automatically flipping the normals for "back" faces within the PBR lighting shader.
fields.unlit: Whether to apply only the base color to this material.
fields.fog_enabled: Whether to enable fog for this material.
fields.alpha_mode: How to apply the alpha channel of the `base_color_texture`.
fields.depth_map: The depth map used for [parallax mapping].
fields.parallax_depth_scale: How deep the offset introduced by the depth map should be.
fields.parallax_mapping_method: Which parallax mapping method to use.
fields.max_parallax_layer_count: In how many layers to split the depth maps for parallax mapping.
fields.lightmap_exposure: The exposure (brightness) level of the lightmap, if present.
fields.opaque_render_method: Render method used for opaque materials. (Where `alpha_mode` is `AlphaMode::Opaque` or `AlphaMode::Mask`)
fields.deferred_lighting_pass_id: Used for selecting the deferred lighting pass for deferred materials. Default is `DEFAULT_PBR_DEFERRED_LIGHTING_PASS_ID` for default PBR deferred lighting pass. Ignored in the case of forward materials.
fields.uv_transform: The transform applied to the UVs corresponding to `ATTRIBUTE_UV_0` on the mesh before sampling. Default is identity.

bevy_pbr::render::mesh::MeshPipeline.doc: All data needed to construct a pipeline for rendering 3D meshes.

fields.view_layouts: A reference to all the mesh pipeline view layouts.
fields.clustered_forward_buffer_binding_type: A reference to all the mesh pipeline view layouts.
fields.mesh_layouts: A reference to all the mesh pipeline view layouts.
fields.per_object_buffer_batch_size: `MeshUniform`s are stored in arrays in buffers. If storage buffers are available, they are used and this will be `None`, otherwise uniform buffers will be used with batches of this many `MeshUniform`s, stored at dynamic offsets within the uniform buffer. Use code like this in custom shaders: ```wesl @if(PER_OBJECT_BUFFER_BATCH_SIZE) @group(1) @binding(0) var<uniform> mesh: array<Mesh, u32(constants::PER_OBJECT_BUFFER_BATCH_SIZE)>; @else @group(1) @binding(0) var<storage> mesh: array<Mesh>; ```
fields.binding_arrays_are_usable: Whether binding arrays (a.k.a. bindless textures) are usable on the current render device.
fields.clustered_decals_are_usable: Whether clustered decals are usable on the current render device.
fields.skins_use_uniform_buffers: Whether skins will use uniform buffers on account of storage buffers being unavailable on this platform.
fields.metadata_use_uniform_buffers: Whether mesh metadata will use uniform buffers on account of storage buffers being unavailable on this platform.

bevy_pbr::ssao::ScreenSpaceAmbientOcclus.doc: Component to apply screen space ambient occlusion to a 3d camera.

fields.radius: Maximum sample distance, in view-space units.
fields.constant_object_thickness: A constant estimated thickness of objects.

bevy_pbr::ssr::ScreenSpaceReflections.doc: Add this component to a camera to enable *screen-space reflections* (SSR).

fields.min_perceptual_roughness: The perceptual roughness range over which SSR begins to fade in.
fields.max_perceptual_roughness: The perceptual roughness range over which SSR begins to fade out.
fields.thickness: When marching the depth buffer, we only have 2.5D information and don't know how thick surfaces are. We shall assume that the depth buffer fragments are cuboids with a constant thickness defined by this parameter.
fields.linear_steps: The number of steps to be taken at regular intervals to find an initial intersection. Must not be zero.
fields.linear_march_exponent: Exponent to be applied in the linear part of the march.
fields.edge_fadeout: The range over which SSR begins to fade out at the edges of the screen, in terms of a percentage of the screen dimensions.
fields.bisection_steps: Number of steps in a bisection (binary search) to perform once the linear search has found an intersection. Helps narrow down the hit, increasing the chance of the secant method finding an accurate hit point.
fields.use_secant: Approximate the root position using the secant method—by solving for line-line intersection between the ray approach rate and the surface gradient.

bevy_pbr::transmission::ScreenSpaceTrans.doc: Configures transmission behavior, offering a trade-off between performance and visual fidelity.

fields.steps: How many individual steps should be performed in the `Transmissive3d` pass.
fields.quality: The quality of the screen space specular transmission blur effect, applied to whatever's behind transmissive objects when their `roughness` is greater than `0.0`.

bevy_pbr::transmission::ScreenSpaceTrans.doc: The quality of the screen space transmission blur effect, applied to whatever's behind transmissive objects when their `roughness` is greater than `0.0`.

fields.Low: Best performance at the cost of quality. Suitable for lower end GPUs. (e.g. Mobile)
fields.Medium: A balanced option between quality and performance.
fields.High: Better quality. Suitable for high end GPUs. (e.g. Desktop)
fields.Ultra: The highest quality, suitable for non-realtime rendering. (e.g. Pre-rendered cinematics and photo mode)

bevy_pbr::wireframe::NoWireframe.doc: Disables wireframe rendering for any entity it is attached to. It will ignore the `WireframeConfig` global setting.

bevy_pbr::wireframe::Wireframe.doc: Enables wireframe rendering for any entity it is attached to. It will ignore the `WireframeConfig` global setting.

bevy_pbr::wireframe::WireframeColor.doc: Sets the color of the `Wireframe` of the entity it is attached to.

fields.global: Whether to show wireframes for all meshes. Can be overridden for individual meshes by adding a `Wireframe` or `NoWireframe` component.
fields.default_color: If `Self::global` is set, any `Entity` that does not have a `Wireframe` component attached to it will have wireframes using this color. Otherwise, this will be the fallback color for any entity that has a `Wireframe`, but no `WireframeColor`.
fields.default_line_width: Default line width in screen-space pixels.
fields.xray_mode: Whether all wireframe pipelines render as x-ray overlays. When enabled, both sides are rendered without depth testing.

bevy_pbr::wireframe::WireframeLineWidth.doc: Sets the line width (in screen-space pixels) of the wireframe.

bevy_pbr::wireframe::WireframeTopology.doc: Controls whether wireframe edges follow triangle or quad topology.

fields.Quads: Does a best-effort attempt to detect quads from a triangle mesh. No guarantee of accuracy is made, that is, there may be both false positives and false negatives in the rendered output.

bevy_pbr::wireframe::WireframeXray.doc: Controls whether wireframe edges render as an x-ray overlay.

bevy_picking::Pickable.doc: An optional component that marks an entity as usable by a backend, and overrides default picking behavior for an entity.

fields.should_block_lower: Should this entity block entities below it from being picked?
fields.is_hoverable: If this is set to `false` and `should_block_lower` is set to true, this entity will block lower entities from being interacted and at the same time will itself not emit any events.

fields.is_enabled: Enables and disables all picking features.
fields.is_hover_enabled: Enables and disables updating interaction states of entities.
fields.is_window_picking_enabled: Enables or disables picking for window entities.
fields.multi_click_interval: Maximum time between presses or clicks for them to count as consecutive.

bevy_picking::backend::HitData.doc: Holds data from a successful pointer hit test. See `HitData::depth` for important details.

fields.camera: The camera entity used to detect this hit. Useful when you need to find the ray that was cast for this hit when using a raycasting backend.
fields.depth: `depth` only needs to be self-consistent with other `PointerHits`s using the same `RenderTarget`. However, it is recommended to use the distance from the pointer to the hit, measured from the near plane of the camera, to the point, in world space.
fields.position: The position reported by the backend, if the data is available. Position data may be in any space (e.g. World space, Screen space, Local space), specified by the backend providing it.
fields.normal: The normal vector of the hit test, if the data is available from the backend.
fields.extra: Optional backend-specific extra data attached to this hit. Read it with `HitData::extra_as`.

fields.map: Cartesian product of all pointers and all cameras Add your rays here to support picking through indirections, e.g. rendered-to-texture cameras

bevy_picking::cursor::DefaultCursor.doc: A resource that specifies the cursor icon to be used when the mouse is not hovering over any other entity. This is used to set the default cursor icon for the window.

bevy_picking::cursor::EntityCursor.doc: A component that specifies the cursor shape to be used when the pointer hovers over an entity. This is copied to the windows's `CursorIcon` component.

bevy_picking::cursor::OverrideCursor.doc: A resource used to override any `EntityCursor` cursor changes.

fields.start_pos: The position of the pointer at drag start.
fields.latest_pos: The latest position of the pointer during this drag, used to compute deltas.

bevy_picking::events::HoveredEntityAnces.doc: A cache map containing the ancestry of hovered entities

bevy_picking::events::PointerButtonState.doc: An entry in the cache that drives the `pointer_events` system, storing additional data about pointer button presses.

bevy_picking::hover::DirectlyHovered.doc: A component that allows users to use regular Bevy change detection to determine when the pointer is directly hovering over an entity. Users should insert this component on an entity to indicate interest in knowing about hover state changes.

bevy_picking::hover::HoverMap.doc: The source of truth for all hover state. This is used to determine what events to send, and what state components should be in.

bevy_picking::hover::Hovered.doc: A component that allows users to use regular Bevy change detection to determine when the pointer enters or leaves an entity. Users should insert this component on an entity to indicate interest in knowing about hover state changes.

bevy_picking::hover::PickingInteraction.doc: A component that aggregates picking interaction state of this entity across all pointers.

fields.Hovered: The entity is being hovered by a pointer.

bevy_post_process::auto_exposure::settin.doc: Component that enables auto exposure for an HDR-enabled 2d or 3d camera.

bevy_post_process::bloom::settings::Bloo.doc: Applies a bloom effect to an HDR-enabled 2d or 3d camera.

fields.intensity: Controls the baseline of how much the image is scattered (default: 0.15).
fields.low_frequency_boost: Low frequency contribution boost. Controls how much more likely the light is to scatter completely sideways (low frequency image).
fields.low_frequency_boost_curvature: Low frequency contribution boost curve. Controls the curvature of the blend factor function making frequencies next to the lowest ones contribute more.
fields.high_pass_frequency: Tightens how much the light scatters (default: 1.0).
fields.prefilter: Controls the threshold filter used for extracting the brightest regions from the input image before blurring them and compositing back onto the original image.
fields.composite_mode: Controls whether bloom textures are blended between or added to each other. Useful if image brightening is desired and a must-change if `prefilter` is used.
fields.max_mip_dimension: Maximum size of each dimension for the largest mipchain texture used in downscaling/upscaling. Only tweak if you are seeing visual artifacts.
fields.scale: Amount to stretch the bloom on each axis. Artistic control, can be used to emulate anamorphic blur by using a large x-value. For large values, you may need to increase `Bloom::max_mip_dimension` to reduce sampling artifacts.

bevy_post_process::bloom::settings::Bloo.doc: Applies a threshold filter to the input image to extract the brightest regions before blurring them and compositing back onto the original image. These settings are useful when emulating the 1990s-2000s game look.

fields.threshold_softness: Controls how much to blend between the thresholded and non-thresholded colors (default: 0.0).

bevy_render::view::ColorGrading.doc: Configures filmic color grading parameters to adjust the image appearance.

fields.global: Filmic color grading values applied to the image as a whole (as opposed to individual sections, like shadows and highlights).
fields.shadows: Color grading values that are applied to the darker parts of the image.
fields.midtones: Color grading values that are applied to the parts of the image with intermediate brightness.
fields.highlights: Color grading values that are applied to the lighter parts of the image.

bevy_render::view::ColorGradingGlobal.doc: Filmic color grading values applied to the image as a whole (as opposed to individual sections, like shadows and highlights).

fields.exposure: Exposure value (EV) offset, measured in stops.
fields.temperature: An adjustment made to the [CIE 1931] chromaticity *x* value.
fields.tint: An adjustment made to the [CIE 1931] chromaticity *y* value.
fields.hue: An adjustment to the [hue], in radians.
fields.post_saturation: Saturation adjustment applied after tonemapping. Values below 1.0 desaturate, with a value of 0.0 resulting in a grayscale image with luminance defined by ITU-R BT.709 Values above 1.0 increase saturation.
fields.midtones_range: The luminance (brightness) ranges that are considered part of the "midtones" of the image.

bevy_render::view::ColorGradingSection.doc: A section of color grading values that can be selectively applied to shadows, midtones, and highlights.

fields.saturation: Values below 1.0 desaturate, with a value of 0.0 resulting in a grayscale image with luminance defined by ITU-R BT.709. Values above 1.0 increase saturation.
fields.gamma: A nonlinear luminance adjustment, mainly affecting the high end of the range.
fields.gain: A linear luminance adjustment, mainly affecting the middle part of the range.
fields.lift: A fixed luminance adjustment, mainly affecting the lower part of the range.

bevy_render::view::DebandDither.doc: Enables a debanding shader that applies dithering to mitigate color banding in the final image for a given `Camera` entity.

bevy_render::view::Msaa.doc: Component for configuring the number of samples for Multi-Sample Anti-Aliasing for a `Camera`.

bevy_render::view::Tonemapping.doc: Optionally enables a tonemapping shader that attempts to map linear input stimulus into a perceptually uniform image for a given `Camera` entity.

fields.None: Bypass tonemapping. No color grading, exposure, or dither applies.
fields.Linear: Identity tone curve. `ColorGrading`, exposure, and `DebandDither` still apply. The output is unbounded display-linear.
fields.Reinhard: Suffers from lots hue shifting, brights don't desaturate naturally. Bright primaries and secondaries don't desaturate at all.
fields.ReinhardLuminance: Suffers from hue shifting. Brights don't desaturate much at all across the spectrum.
fields.AcesFitted: Same base implementation that Godot 4.0 uses for Tonemap ACES. <https://github.com/TheRealMJP/BakingLab/blob/master/BakingLab/ACES.hlsl> Not neutral, has a very specific aesthetic, intentional and dramatic hue shifting. Bright greens and reds turn orange. Bright blues turn magenta. Significantly increased contrast. Brights desaturate across the spectrum.
fields.AgX: By Troy Sobotka <https://github.com/sobotka/AgX> Very neutral. Image is somewhat desaturated when compared to other tonemappers. Little to no hue shifting. Subtle Abney shifting. NOTE: Requires the `tonemapping_luts` cargo feature.
fields.SomewhatBoringDisplayTransform: By Tomasz Stachowiak Has little hue shifting in the darks and mids, but lots in the brights. Brights desaturate across the spectrum. Is sort of between Reinhard and `ReinhardLuminance`. Conceptually similar to reinhard-jodie. Designed as a compromise if you want e.g. decent skin tones in low light, but can't afford to re-do your VFX to look good without hue shifting.
fields.TonyMcMapface: Current Bevy default. By Tomasz Stachowiak <https://github.com/h3r2tic/tony-mc-mapface> Very neutral. Subtle but intentional hue shifting. Brights desaturate across the spectrum. Comment from author: Tony is a display transform intended for real-time applications such as games. It is intentionally boring, does not increase contrast or saturation, and stays close to the input stimulus where compression isn't necessary. Brightness-equivalent luminance of the input stimulus is compressed. The non-linearity resembles Reinhard. Color hues are preserved during compression, except for a deliberate Bezold–Brücke shift. To avoid posterization, selective desaturation is employed, with care to avoid the Abney effect. NOTE: Requires the `tonemapping_luts` cargo feature.
fields.BlenderFilmic: Default Filmic Display Transform from blender. Somewhat neutral. Suffers from hue shifting. Brights desaturate across the spectrum. NOTE: Requires the `tonemapping_luts` cargo feature.
fields.KhronosPbrNeutral: Despite its name, it is not considered to be neutral. Highly saturated colors and tends to produce a very high contrast image. Suffers from significant Abney shifting, and tends to crush grays and desaturated colors. Designed for e-commerce to faithfully reproduce the colors of brand's logos when used with low brightness grayscale lighting. See the KhronosGroup spec for more information.

fields.max_bounces: Maximum number of bounces traced when generating an initial path.

fields.world_cache_max_gi_ray_distance: Maximum distance to trace GI rays between two world cache cells.
fields.world_cache_cell_updates_soft_target: Soft upper limit on the number of world cache cells to update each frame.

bevy_solari::scene::types::RaytracingMes.doc: A mesh component used for raytracing.

bevy_sprite::picking_backend::SpritePick.doc: An optional component that marks cameras that should be used in the `SpritePickingPlugin`.
How should the `SpritePickingPlugin` handle picking and how should it handle transparent pixels

bevy_sprite::sprite::Anchor.doc: Normalized (relative to its size) offset of a 2d renderable entity from its `Transform`.

bevy_sprite::sprite::Sprite.doc: Describes a sprite to be rendered to a 2D camera

fields.image: The image used to render the sprite
fields.texture_atlas: The (optional) texture atlas used to render the sprite
fields.flip_x: Flip the sprite along the `X` axis
fields.flip_y: Flip the sprite along the `Y` axis
fields.custom_size: An optional custom size for the sprite that will be used when rendering, instead of the size of the sprite's image
