bevy_sprite::sprite::SpriteAlphaMode.doc: An enum describing how a sprite's alpha channel will be handled. The base color being modified is that of the texture after tinting. The default is `Blend`.

fields.Opaque: Base color alpha values are overridden to be fully opaque (1.0).
fields.Mask: Reduce transparency to fully opaque or fully transparent based on a threshold.
fields.Blend: The base color alpha value defines the opacity of the color. Standard alpha-blending is used to blend the fragment's color with the color behind it.

bevy_sprite::sprite::SpriteImageMode.doc: Controls how the image is altered when scaled.

fields.Auto: The sprite will take on the size of the image by default, and will be stretched or shrunk if `Sprite::custom_size` is set.
fields.Scale: The texture will be scaled to fit the rect bounds defined in `Sprite::custom_size`. Otherwise no scaling will be applied.
fields.Sliced: The texture will be cut in 9 slices, keeping the texture in proportions on resize
fields.Tiled: The texture will be repeated if stretched beyond `stretched_value`

bevy_sprite::sprite::SpriteScalingMode.doc: Represents various modes for proportional scaling of a texture.

fields.FillCenter: Scale the texture uniformly (maintain the texture's aspect ratio) so that both dimensions (width and height) of the texture will be equal to or larger than the corresponding dimension of the target rectangle. Fill sprite with a centered texture.
fields.FillStart: Scales the texture to fill the target rectangle while maintaining its aspect ratio. One dimension of the texture will match the rectangle's size, while the other dimension may exceed it. The exceeding portion is aligned to the start: * Horizontal overflow is left-aligned if the width exceeds the rectangle. * Vertical overflow is top-aligned if the height exceeds the rectangle.
fields.FillEnd: Scales the texture to fill the target rectangle while maintaining its aspect ratio. One dimension of the texture will match the rectangle's size, while the other dimension may exceed it. The exceeding portion is aligned to the end: * Horizontal overflow is right-aligned if the width exceeds the rectangle. * Vertical overflow is bottom-aligned if the height exceeds the rectangle.
fields.FitCenter: Scaling the texture will maintain the original aspect ratio and ensure that the original texture fits entirely inside the rect. At least one axis (x or y) will fit exactly. The result is centered inside the rect.
fields.FitStart: Scaling the texture will maintain the original aspect ratio and ensure that the original texture fits entirely inside rect. At least one axis (x or y) will fit exactly. Aligns the result to the left and top edges of rect.
fields.FitEnd: Scaling the texture will maintain the original aspect ratio and ensure that the original texture fits entirely inside rect. At least one axis (x or y) will fit exactly. Aligns the result to the right and bottom edges of rect.

fields.offset: Shadow displacement With a value of zero the shadow will be hidden directly behind the text

bevy_sprite::texture_slice::slicer::Slic.doc: Defines how a texture slice scales when resized

bevy_sprite::texture_slice::slicer::Text.doc: Slices a texture using the **9-slicing** technique. This allows to reuse an image at various sizes without needing to prepare multiple assets. fields.border: Inset values in pixels that define the four slicing lines dividing the texture into nine sections.
fields.center_scale_mode: Defines how the center part of the 9 slices will scale
fields.sides_scale_mode: Defines how the 4 side parts of the 9 slices will scale
fields.max_corner_scale: Defines the maximum scale of the 4 corner slices (default to `1.0`)

bevy_text::text::LineBreak.doc: Determines how lines will be broken when preventing text from running out of bounds.

bevy_ui::Node.doc: The base component for UI entities. It describes UI layout and style properties.

fields.display: Which layout algorithm to use when laying out this node's contents: - `Display::Flex`: Use the Flexbox layout algorithm - `Display::Grid`: Use the CSS Grid layout algorithm - `Display::None`: Hide this node and perform layout as if it does not exist.
fields.box_sizing: Which part of a Node's box length styles like width and height control - `BoxSizing::BorderBox`: They refer to the "border box" size (size including padding and border) - `BoxSizing::ContentBox`: They refer to the "content box" size (size excluding padding and border)
fields.position_type: Whether a node should be laid out in-flow with, or independently of its siblings: - `PositionType::Relative`: Layout this node in-flow with other nodes using the usual (flexbox/grid) layout algorithm. - `PositionType::Absolute`: Layout this node on top and independently of other nodes.
fields.overflow: Whether overflowing content should be displayed or clipped.
fields.scrollbar_width: How much space in logical pixels should be reserved for scrollbars when overflow is set to scroll or auto on an axis.
fields.overflow_clip_margin: How the bounds of clipped content should be determined
fields.left: The horizontal position of the left edge of the node. - For relatively positioned nodes, this is relative to the node's position as computed during regular layout. - For absolutely positioned nodes, this is relative to the *parent* node's bounding box.
fields.right: The horizontal position of the right edge of the node. - For relatively positioned nodes, this is relative to the node's position as computed during regular layout. - For absolutely positioned nodes, this is relative to the *parent* node's bounding box.
fields.top: The vertical position of the top edge of the node. - For relatively positioned nodes, this is relative to the node's position as computed during regular layout. - For absolutely positioned nodes, this is relative to the *parent* node's bounding box.
fields.bottom: The vertical position of the bottom edge of the node. - For relatively positioned nodes, this is relative to the node's position as computed during regular layout. - For absolutely positioned nodes, this is relative to the *parent* node's bounding box.
fields.width: The ideal width of the node. `width` is used when it is within the bounds defined by `min_width` and `max_width`.
fields.height: The ideal height of the node. `height` is used when it is within the bounds defined by `min_height` and `max_height`.
fields.min_width: The minimum width of the node. `min_width` is used if it is greater than `width` and/or `max_width`.
fields.min_height: The minimum height of the node. `min_height` is used if it is greater than `height` and/or `max_height`.
fields.max_width: The maximum width of the node. `max_width` is used if it is within the bounds defined by `min_width` and `width`.
fields.max_height: The maximum height of the node. `max_height` is used if it is within the bounds defined by `min_height` and `height`.
fields.aspect_ratio: The aspect ratio of the node (defined as `width / height`)
fields.align_items: Used to control how each individual item is aligned by default within the space they're given. - For Flexbox containers, sets default cross axis alignment of the child items. - For CSS Grid containers, controls block (vertical) axis alignment of children of this grid container within their grid areas.
fields.justify_items: Used to control how each individual item is aligned by default within the space they're given. - For Flexbox containers, this property has no effect. See `justify_content` for main axis alignment of flex items. - For CSS Grid containers, sets default inline (horizontal) axis alignment of child items within their grid areas.
fields.align_self: Used to control how the specified item is aligned within the space it's given. - For Flexbox items, controls cross axis alignment of the item. - For CSS Grid items, controls block (vertical) axis alignment of a grid item within its grid area.
fields.justify_self: Used to control how the specified item is aligned within the space it's given. - For Flexbox items, this property has no effect. See `justify_content` for main axis alignment of flex items. - For CSS Grid items, controls inline (horizontal) axis alignment of a grid item within its grid area.
fields.align_content: Used to control how items are distributed. - For Flexbox containers, controls alignment of lines if `flex_wrap` is set to `FlexWrap::Wrap` and there are multiple lines of items. - For CSS Grid containers, controls alignment of grid rows.
fields.justify_content: Used to control how items are distributed. - For Flexbox containers, controls alignment of items in the main axis. - For CSS Grid containers, controls alignment of grid columns.
fields.direction: Sets the inline axis direction (LTR or RTL) used for layout.
fields.margin: The amount of space around a node outside its border.
fields.padding: The amount of space between the edges of a node and its contents.
fields.border: The amount of space between the margins of a node and its padding.
fields.border_radius: Used to add rounded corners to a UI node. You can set a UI node to have uniformly rounded corners or specify different radii for each corner. If a given radius exceeds half the length of the smallest dimension between the node's height or width, the radius will calculated as half the smallest dimension.

fields.FlexEnd: The items are packed towards the end of the axis, unless the flex direction is reversed; then the items are packed towards the start of the axis.
fields.Center: The items are packed along the center of the axis.
fields.Stretch: The items are stretched to fill the container along the axis.
fields.SpaceBetween: The items are distributed such that the gap between any two items is equal.

bevy_ui::ui_node::Node.doc: The base component for UI entities. It describes UI layout and style properties.

fields.scrollbar_width: How much space in logical pixels should be reserved for scrollbars when overflow is set to scroll or auto on an axis.

fields.right: The horizontal position of the right edge of the node. - For relatively positioned nodes, this is relative to the node's position as computed during regular layout. - For absolutely positioned nodes, this is relative to the *parent* node's bounding box.

fields.height: The ideal height of the node. `height` is used when it is within the bounds defined by `min_height` and `max_height`.

fields.min_height: The minimum height of the node. `min_height` is used if it is greater than `height` and/or `max_height`.
fields.max_width: The maximum width of the node. `max_width` is used if it is within the bounds defined by `min_width` and `width`.
fields.max_height: The maximum height of the node. `max_height` is used if it is within the bounds defined by `min_height` and `height`.

fields.align_items: Used to control how each individual item is aligned by default within the space they're given. - For Flexbox containers, sets default cross axis alignment of the child items. - For CSS Grid containers, controls block (vertical) axis alignment of children of this grid container within their grid areas.

See `justify_content` for main axis alignment of flex items. - For CSS Grid containers, sets default inline (horizontal) axis alignment of child items within their grid areas.

fields.justify_self: Used to control how the specified item is aligned within the space it's given. - For Flexbox items, this property has no effect. See `justify_content` for main axis alignment of flex items. - For CSS Grid items, controls inline (horizontal) axis alignment of a grid item within its grid area.
fields.align_content: Used to control how items are distributed. - For Flexbox containers, controls alignment of lines if `flex_wrap` is set to `FlexWrap::Wrap` and there are multiple lines of items. - For CSS Grid containers, controls alignment of grid rows.
fields.justify_content: Used to control how items are distributed. - For Flexbox containers, controls alignment of items in the main axis. - For CSS Grid containers, controls alignment of grid columns.
fields.direction: Sets the inline axis direction (LTR or RTL) used for layout.
fields.margin: The amount of space around a node outside its border.
fields.padding: The amount of space between the edges of a node and its contents.
fields.border: The amount of space between the margins of a node and its padding.
fields.border_radius: Used to add rounded corners to a UI node. You can set a UI node to have uniformly rounded corners or specify different radii for each corner. If a given radius exceeds half the length of the smallest dimension between the node's height or width, the radius will calculated as half the smallest dimension.
fields.flex_direction: Whether a Flexbox container should be a row or a column. This property has no effect on Grid nodes.
fields.flex_wrap: Whether a Flexbox container should wrap its contents onto multiple lines if they overflow. This property has no effect on Grid nodes.
fields.flex_grow: Defines how much a flexbox item should grow if there's space available. Defaults to 0 (don't grow at all).
fields.flex_shrink: Defines how much a flexbox item should shrink if there's not enough space available. Defaults to 1.
fields.flex_basis: The initial length of a flexbox in the main axis, before flex growing/shrinking properties are applied.
fields.row_gap: The size of the gutters between items in a vertical flexbox layout or between rows in a grid layout.
fields.column_gap: The size of the gutters between items in a horizontal flexbox layout or between column in a grid layout.
fields.grid_auto_flow: Controls whether automatically placed grid items are placed row-wise or column-wise as well as whether the sparse or dense packing algorithm is used. Only affects Grid layouts.
fields.grid_template_rows: Defines the number of rows a grid has and the sizes of those rows. If grid items are given explicit placements then more rows may be implicitly generated by items that are placed out of bounds. The sizes of those rows are controlled by `grid_auto_rows` property.
fields.grid_template_columns: Defines the number of columns a grid has and the sizes of those columns. If grid items are given explicit placements then more columns may be implicitly generated by items that are placed out of bounds. The sizes of those columns are controlled by `grid_auto_columns` property.
fields.grid_auto_rows: Defines the size of implicitly created rows. Rows are created implicitly when grid items are given explicit placements that are out of bounds of the rows explicitly created using `grid_template_rows`.
fields.grid_auto_columns: Defines the size of implicitly created columns. Columns are created implicitly when grid items are given explicit placements that are out of bounds of the columns explicitly created using `grid_template_columns`.
fields.grid_row: The row in which a grid item starts and how many rows it spans.
fields.grid_column: The column in which a grid item starts and how many columns it spans.

bevy_ui::ui_node::OuterColor.doc: Sets a color to fill the regions outside the Node's border created when a border radius is set.

bevy_ui::ui_node::Outline.doc: The `Outline` component adds an outline outside the edge of a UI node. Outlines do not take up space in the layout.

fields.offset: The amount of space between a node's outline the edge of the node.

bevy_ui::ui_node::Overflow.doc: Whether to show or hide overflowing items

fields.x: Whether to show or clip overflowing items on the x axis
fields.y: Whether to show or clip overflowing items on the y axis

bevy_ui::ui_node::OverflowAxis.doc: Whether to show or hide overflowing items

fields.Hidden: Hide overflowing items by influencing layout and then clipping.

bevy_ui::ui_node::OverflowClipMargin.doc: The bounds of the visible area when a UI node is clipped.

fields.margin: Width of the margin on each edge of the visual box in logical pixels. The width of the margin will be zero if a negative value is set.

bevy_ui::ui_node::OverrideClip.doc: UI node entities with this component will ignore any clipping rect they inherit, the node will not be clipped regardless of its ancestors' `Overflow` setting.

bevy_ui::ui_node::PositionType.doc: The strategy used to position this node

fields.Relative: Relative to all other nodes with the `PositionType::Relative` value.
fields.Absolute: Independent of all other nodes, but relative to its parent node.

bevy_ui::ui_node::ResolvedBorderRadius.doc: Represents the resolved border radii values for a UI node.

bevy_ui::ui_node::ScrollPosition.doc: The scroll position of the node. Values are in logical pixels, increasing from top-left to bottom-right.

fields.spread_radius: How much the shadow should spread outward.

bevy_ui::ui_node::UiTargetCamera.doc: Indicates that this root `Node` entity should be rendered to a specific camera.

bevy_ui::ui_node::VisualBox.doc: Used to determine which region of a UI node is used for visual bounds.

bevy_ui::ui_node::ZIndex.doc: Indicates that this `Node` entity's front-to-back ordering is not controlled solely by its location in the UI hierarchy. A node with a higher z-index will appear on top of sibling nodes with a lower z-index.

fields.scale: Scale the node. A negative value reflects the node in that axis.

bevy_ui::ui_transform::Val2.doc: A pair of `Val`s used to represent a 2-dimensional size or offset.

fields.x: Translate the node along the x-axis. `Val::Percent` values are resolved based on the computed width of the Ui Node. `Val::Auto` is resolved to `0.`.
fields.y: Translate the node along the y-axis. `Val::Percent` values are resolved based on the computed height of the UI Node. `Val::Auto` is resolved to `0.`.

fields.color: The tint color used to draw the image.
fields.width: Set a fixed width in logical pixels for the image's inline box target.
fields.height: Set a fixed height in logical pixels for the image's inline box target.
fields.flip_x: Flip the image on the x-axis.
fields.flip_y: Flip the image on the y-axis.

bevy_ui::widget::image::ImageNode.doc: A UI Node that renders an image.

fields.color: The tint color used to draw the image.
fields.texture_atlas: The (optional) texture atlas used to render the image.
fields.flip_x: Whether the image should be flipped along its x-axis.
fields.flip_y: Whether the image should be flipped along its y-axis.
fields.rect: An optional rectangle representing the region of the image to render, instead of rendering the full image. This is an easy one-off alternative to using a `TextureAtlas`.
fields.image_mode: Controls how the image is altered to fit within the layout and how the layout algorithm determines the space to allocate for the image.
fields.visual_box: Which region of the UI node the image should be drawn within.

bevy_ui::widget::image::ImageNodeSize.doc: The size of the image's texture

bevy_ui::widget::image::NodeImageMode.doc: Controls how the image is altered to fit within the layout and how the layout algorithm determines the space in the layout for the image

fields.Auto: The image will be sized automatically by taking the size of the source image and applying any layout constraints.
fields.Stretch: The image will be resized to match the size of the node. The image's original size and aspect ratio will be ignored.
fields.Sliced: The texture will be cut in 9 slices, keeping the texture in proportions on resize
fields.Tiled: The texture will be repeated if stretched beyond `stretched_value`

fields.color: The tint color used to draw the image.
fields.width: Set a fixed width in logical pixels for the image's inline box target.
fields.height: Set a fixed height in logical pixels for the image's inline box target.
fields.flip_x: Flip the image on the x-axis.
fields.flip_y: Flip the image on the y-axis.

fields.offset: Shadow displacement in logical pixels With a value of zero the shadow will be hidden directly behind the text

bevy_ui::widget::viewport::ViewportNode.doc: Component used to render a `RenderTarget`  to a node.

fields.camera: The entity representing the `Camera` associated with this viewport.

bevy_ui_render::BoxShadowSamples.doc: Number of shadow samples. A larger value will result in higher quality shadows. Default is 4, values higher than ~10 offer diminishing returns.

bevy_ui_widgets::Activate.doc: Notification sent by a button or menu item.

fields.Horizontal: Horizontal orientation (stretching from left to right)
fields.Vertical: Vertical orientation (stretching from top to bottom)

bevy_ui_widgets::Scrollbar.doc: A headless scrollbar widget, which can be used to build custom scrollbars.

fields.orientation: Whether the scrollbar is vertical or horizontal.
fields.min_thumb_length: Minimum length of the scrollbar thumb, in pixel units, in the direction parallel to the main scrollbar axis. The scrollbar will resize the thumb entity based on the proportion of visible size to content size, but no smaller than this. This prevents the thumb from disappearing in cases where the ratio of content size to visible size is large.

bevy_ui_widgets::ScrollbarThumb.doc: This component indicates that the entity is a scrollbar thumb (the moving, draggable part of the scrollbar). This should be a child of the scrollbar entity.

fields.border_radius: Border radius of the scrollbar thumb, used to update `ComputedNode::border_radius` in `UiSystems::Layout`.
fields.border: Thickness of the thumb node's border.

bevy_ui_widgets::button::ActivateOnPress.doc: Optional marker component that indicates we want the button to activate on the pointer down event, this is used for menu buttons.

bevy_ui_widgets::button::Button.doc: Headless button widget. This widget maintains a "pressed" state, which is used to indicate whether the button is currently being pressed by the user. It emits an `Activate` event when the button is un-pressed.

bevy_ui_widgets::checkbox::Checkbox.doc: Headless widget implementation for checkboxes. The `Checked` component represents the current state of the checkbox. The widget will emit a `ValueChange<bool>` event when clicked, or when the `Enter` or `Space` key is pressed while the checkbox is focused.

bevy_ui_widgets::checkbox::SetChecked.doc: Event which can be triggered on a checkbox to set the checked state. This can be used to control the checkbox via gamepad buttons or other inputs.

fields.entity: The `Checkbox` entity to set the "checked" state on.

bevy_ui_widgets::checkbox::ToggleChecked.doc: Event which can be triggered on a checkbox to toggle the checked state. This can be used to control the checkbox via gamepad buttons or other inputs.

bevy_ui_widgets::dialog::Dialog.doc: A dialog box. When `ModalDialog` is also present it traps focus and is backed by a `crate::ModalDialogBarrier`; when absent it is a movable, non-blocking floating window.

bevy_ui_widgets::dialog::DialogDragHandl.doc: Marks a region (e.g. a title bar) that drags its owning `Dialog`.

bevy_ui_widgets::dialog::DialogDragState.doc: Records the owning dialog's translation when a drag begins, so each drag event can set an absolute position from the drag's cumulative distance.

bevy_ui_widgets::dialog::RequestClose.doc: Event used to indicate that the dialog wants to be closed. This can happen because the user clicked on the barrier, hit the escape key, or clicked the close box in the dialog title. This event propagates so that the owner of the dialog can despawn it.

bevy_ui_widgets::list::ActiveDescendant.doc: Component used for keyboard navigation. Individual rows should not be focusable in the normal way, as this would make tabbing through a long list tedious. Instead, we track the current "active" row separately using a component on the list box. The active row will be displayed with an outline.

bevy_ui_widgets::list::ListItem.doc: Headless widget implementation for listbox items. These should be enclosed within a `ListBox` widget, which is responsible for the mutual exclusion logic.

bevy_ui_widgets::list::ReselectListRow.doc: Notification sent by a `ListBox` when the user commits the already-selected item, either by clicking it or by pressing Space/Enter while it is the active row. No `ValueChange` is emitted in this case, since the selection did not change. Used in for example a popup select control to close the popup when reselecting

fields.source: The listbox that produced this event.

bevy_ui_widgets::list::SetSelected.doc: Programmatically set which entity is selected (a single row of the list) Wraps a call to send `ValueChange`. No-op if already selected or disabled

fields.row: The child to set value to

fields.Open: Indicates we want to open the menu, if it is not already open, and focus the first or last item depending on the `NavAction`.
fields.Toggle: Open the menu if it's closed, close it if it's open. Generally sent from a menu button.
fields.FocusRoot: Set focus to the menu button or other owner of the popup stack. This happens when the menu is closed by pressing the escape key.

bevy_ui_widgets::menu::MenuButton.doc: Headless menu button widget. This is meant to be combined with the `Button` component, and adds a few more key codes - arrow keys to open the popup.

bevy_ui_widgets::menu::MenuEvent.doc: Event used to control the state of the open menu. This bubbles upwards from the menu items and the menu container, through the portal relation, and to the menu owner entity.

fields.source: The `MenuItem` or `MenuPopup` that triggered this event.
fields.action: The desired action in response to this event.

bevy_ui_widgets::menu::MenuFocusState.doc: Component used to manage focus on the popup. Menu popups remain open only so long as they contain focus.

fields.Opening: A newly opened menu, which needs to have focus set to the first or last item depending on `NavAction`.
fields.Open: Menu is open, and focus is set to an item within the menu
fields.Closed: Menu is no longer visible, and can be cleaned up.

bevy_ui_widgets::menu::MenuItem.doc: Component that defines a menu item.

bevy_ui_widgets::menu::MenuLayout.doc: Specifies the layout direction of the menu, for keyboard navigation

fields.Column: A vertical stack. Up and down arrows to move between items.
fields.Row: A horizontal row. Left and right arrows to move between items.
fields.Grid: A 2D grid. Arrow keys are not mapped, you'll need to write your own observer.

bevy_ui_widgets::menu::MenuPopup.doc: Component that defines a popup menu container.

fields.layout: The layout orientation of the menu

bevy_ui_widgets::modal::ModalDialog.doc: Component that defines a modal dialog box.

bevy_ui_widgets::modal::ModalDialogBarri.doc: Component that defines the barrier element that covers the screen behind the dialog box.

bevy_ui_widgets::popover::Popover.doc: Component which is inserted into a popover element to make it dynamically position relative to an parent element.

fields.positions: List of potential positions for the popover element relative to the parent.
fields.window_margin: Indicates how close to the window edge the popup is allowed to go.

bevy_ui_widgets::popover::PopoverAlign.doc: How the popover element should be aligned to the parent element. The alignment will be along an axis that is perpendicular to the direction of the popover side. So for example, if the popup is positioned below the parent, then the `PopoverAlign` variant controls the horizontal alignment of the popup.

fields.Start: The starting edge of the popover element should be aligned to the starting edge of the parent.
fields.Center: The center of the popover element should be aligned to the center of the parent.
fields.End: The ending edge of the popover element should be aligned to the ending edge of the parent.

bevy_ui_widgets::popover::PopoverPlaceme.doc: Indicates a possible position of a popover element relative to it's parent. You can specify multiple possible positions; the positioning code will check to see if there is sufficient space to display the popup without being clipped by the window edge. If any position has sufficient room, it will pick the first one; if there are none, then it will pick the least bad one.

fields.side: The side of the parent entity where the popover element should be placed.
fields.align: How the popover element should be aligned to the parent entity.
fields.gap: The size of the gap between the parent and the popover element, in logical pixels. This will offset the popover along the direction of `side`.

bevy_ui_widgets::popover::PopoverSide.doc: Which side of the parent element the popover element should be placed.

fields.Top: The popover element should be placed above the parent.
fields.Bottom: The popover element should be placed below the parent.
fields.Left: The popover element should be placed to the left of the parent.
fields.Right: The popover element should be placed to the right of the parent.

bevy_ui_widgets::radio::RadioButton.doc: Headless widget implementation for radio buttons. They can be used independently, but enclosing them in a `RadioGroup` widget allows them to behave as a single, mutually exclusive unit.

bevy_ui_widgets::radio::RadioGroup.doc: Headless widget implementation for a "radio button group". This component is used to group multiple `RadioButton` components together, allowing them to behave as a single unit. It implements the tab navigation logic and keyboard shortcuts for radio buttons.

bevy_ui_widgets::scrollarea::ScrollArea.doc: Marker component to enable trackpad / mouse wheel scrolling. This should be placed on an entity that has overflow: scroll.

fields.Horizontal: Horizontal orientation (stretching from left to right)
fields.Vertical: Vertical orientation (stretching from top to bottom)

bevy_ui_widgets::scrollbar::Scrollbar.doc: A headless scrollbar widget, which can be used to build custom scrollbars.

fields.orientation: Whether the scrollbar is vertical or horizontal.
fields.min_thumb_length: Minimum length of the scrollbar thumb, in pixel units, in the direction parallel to the main scrollbar axis. The scrollbar will resize the thumb entity based on the proportion of visible size to content size, but no smaller than this. This prevents the thumb from disappearing in cases where the ratio of content size to visible size is large.

bevy_ui_widgets::scrollbar::ScrollbarDra.doc: Component used to manage the state of a scrollbar during dragging. This component is inserted on the thumb entity.

fields.dragging: Whether the scrollbar is currently being dragged.

bevy_ui_widgets::scrollbar::ScrollbarThu.doc: This component indicates that the entity is a scrollbar thumb (the moving, draggable part of the scrollbar). This should be a child of the scrollbar entity.

fields.border_radius: Border radius of the scrollbar thumb, used to update `ComputedNode::border_radius` in `UiSystems::Layout`.
fields.border: Thickness of the thumb node's border.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::SetSliderValue.doc: An `EntityEvent` that can be triggered on a slider to modify its value (it will actually trigger a `ValueChange` event, hooking up a corresponding change to `SliderValue` is still the app's responsibility, see `slider_self_update`). This can be used to control the slider via gamepad buttons or other inputs. The value will be clamped when the event is processed.

fields.change: The change to apply to the slider entity.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::Slider.doc: A headless slider widget, which can be used to build custom sliders. Sliders have a value (represented by the `SliderValue` component) and a range (represented by `SliderRange`). An optional step size can be specified via `SliderStep`, and you can control the rounding during dragging with `SliderPrecision`.

fields.track_click: Set the track-clicking behavior for this slider.
fields.orientation: Set the slider orientation. Defaults to auto-detection based on dimensions.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::SliderDragState.doc: Component used to manage the state of a slider during dragging.

fields.dragging: Whether the slider is currently being dragged.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::SliderOrientati.doc: Controls the orientation of the slider.

fields.Auto: Automatically detect orientation based on the slider's dimensions. If height > width, the slider is vertical; otherwise, horizontal.
fields.Horizontal: Force horizontal orientation regardless of dimensions.
fields.Vertical: Force vertical orientation regardless of dimensions.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::SliderPrecision.doc: A component which controls the rounding of the slider value during dragging.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::SliderRange.doc: A component which represents the allowed range of the slider value. Defaults to 0.0..=1.0.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::SliderStep.doc: Defines the amount by which to increment or decrement the slider value when using keyboard shortcuts. Defaults to 1.0.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::SliderThumb.doc: Marker component that identifies which descendant element is the slider thumb.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::SliderValue.doc: A component which stores the current value of the slider.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::SliderValueChan.doc: The type of slider value change to apply in `SetSliderValue`.

fields.Absolute: Set the slider value to a specific value.
fields.Relative: Add a delta to the slider value.
fields.RelativeStep: Add a delta to the slider value, multiplied by the step size.

bevy_ui_widgets::slider::TrackClick.doc: Defines how the slider should behave when you click on the track (not the thumb).

fields.Drag: Clicking on the track lets you drag to edit the value, just like clicking on the thumb.
fields.Step: Clicking on the track increments or decrements the slider by `SliderStep`.
fields.Snap: Clicking on the track snaps the value to the clicked position.

bevy_ui_widgets::tabs::TabActivation.doc: Determines whether moving keyboard focus also requests tab selection.

fields.Manual: Enter or Space requests selection of the focused tab.
fields.Automatic: Moving focus with a navigation key requests selection of the focused tab.

fields.orientation: The axis used by arrow-key navigation.
fields.activation: Whether keyboard navigation requests selection immediately.

bevy_ui_widgets::text_input::SelectAllOn.doc: Marker component for `EditableText` widgets that should select all text on focus.

bevy_window::cursor::CursorIcon.doc: Insert into a window entity to set the cursor for that window.

fields.Image: Use an image as the cursor.
fields.Url: Use a URL to an image as the cursor. Note that this currently only works on the web.

bevy_window::cursor::custom_cursor::Cust.doc: A custom cursor created from an image.

fields.handle: Handle to the image to use as the cursor. The image must be in 8 bit int or 32 bit float rgba. PNG images work well for this.
fields.texture_atlas: An optional texture atlas used to render the image.
fields.flip_x: Whether the image should be flipped along its x-axis.
fields.flip_y: Whether the image should be flipped along its y-axis.
fields.rect: An optional rectangle representing the region of the image to render, instead of rendering the full image. This is an easy one-off alternative to using a `TextureAtlas`.
fields.hotspot: X and Y coordinates of the hotspot in pixels. The hotspot must be within the image bounds.

bevy_window::cursor::custom_cursor::Cust.doc: A custom cursor created from a URL. Note that this currently only works on the web.

fields.url: Web URL to an image to use as the cursor. PNGs are preferred. Cursor creation can fail if the image is invalid or not reachable.
fields.hotspot: X and Y coordinates of the hotspot in pixels. The hotspot must be within the image bounds.

bevy_window::cursor::system_cursor::Syst.doc: The icon to display for a window.

fields.Default: The platform-dependent default cursor. Often rendered as arrow.
fields.ContextMenu: A context menu is available for the object under the cursor. Often rendered as an arrow with a small menu-like graphic next to it.
fields.Help: Help is available for the object under the cursor. Often rendered as a question mark or a balloon.
fields.Pointer: The cursor is a pointer that indicates a link. Often rendered as the backside of a hand with the index finger extended.
fields.Progress: A progress indicator. The program is performing some processing, but is different from `SystemCursorIcon::Wait` in that the user may still interact with the program.
fields.Wait: Indicates that the program is busy and the user should wait. Often rendered as a watch or hourglass.
fields.Cell: Indicates that a cell or set of cells may be selected. Often rendered as a thick plus-sign with a dot in the middle.
fields.Crosshair: A simple crosshair (e.g., short line segments resembling a "+" sign). Often used to indicate a two dimensional bitmap selection mode.
fields.Text: Indicates text that may be selected. Often rendered as an I-beam.
fields.VerticalText: Indicates vertical-text that may be selected. Often rendered as a horizontal I-beam.
fields.Alias: Indicates an alias of/shortcut to something is to be created. Often rendered as an arrow with a small curved arrow next to it.
fields.Copy: Indicates something is to be copied. Often rendered as an arrow with a small plus sign next to it.
fields.Move: Indicates something is to be moved.
fields.NoDrop: Indicates that the dragged item cannot be dropped at the current cursor location. Often rendered as a hand or pointer with a small circle with a line through it.
fields.NotAllowed: Indicates that the requested action will not be carried out. Often rendered as a circle with a line through it.
fields.Grab: Indicates that something can be grabbed (dragged to be moved). Often rendered as the backside of an open hand.
fields.Grabbing: Indicates that something is being grabbed (dragged to be moved). Often rendered as the backside of a hand with fingers closed mostly out of view.
fields.EResize: The east border to be moved.
fields.NResize: The north border to be moved.
fields.NeResize: The north-east corner to be moved.
fields.NwResize: The north-west corner to be moved.
fields.SResize: The south border to be moved.
fields.SeResize: The south-east corner to be moved.
fields.SwResize: The south-west corner to be moved.
fields.WResize: The west border to be moved.
fields.EwResize: The east and west borders to be moved.
fields.NsResize: The south and north borders to be moved.
fields.NeswResize: The north-east and south-west corners to be moved.
fields.NwseResize: The north-west and south-east corners to be moved.
fields.ColResize: Indicates that the item/column can be resized horizontally. Often rendered as arrows pointing left and right with a vertical bar separating them.
fields.RowResize: Indicates that the item/row can be resized vertically. Often rendered as arrows pointing up and down with a horizontal bar separating them.
fields.AllScroll: Indicates that the something can be scrolled in any direction. Often rendered as arrows pointing up, down, left, and right with a dot in the middle.
fields.ZoomIn: Indicates that something can be zoomed in. Often rendered as a magnifying glass with a "+" in the center of the glass.
fields.ZoomOut: Indicates that something can be zoomed in. Often rendered as a magnifying glass with a "-" in the center of the glass.

fields.Idle: The application is not started yet.
fields.WillSuspend: The application is going to be suspended. Applications have one frame to react to this event before being paused in the background.
fields.WillResume: The application is going to be resumed. Applications have one extra frame to react to this event before being fully resumed.

bevy_window::event::CursorEntered.doc: An event that is sent whenever the user's cursor enters a window.

bevy_window::event::CursorLeft.doc: An event that is sent whenever the user's cursor leaves a window.

bevy_window::event::CursorMoved.doc: An event reporting that the mouse cursor has moved inside a window.

fields.window: Window that the cursor moved inside.
fields.position: The cursor position in logical pixels.

bevy_window::event::FileDragAndDrop.doc: Events related to files being dragged and dropped on a window.

fields.DroppedFile: File is being dropped into a window.
fields.HoveredFile: File is currently being hovered over a window.

fields.Preedit: Notifies when a new composing text should be set at the cursor position.
fields.Commit: Notifies when text should be inserted into the editor widget.
fields.Enabled: Notifies when the IME was enabled.
fields.Disabled: Notifies when the IME was disabled.

bevy_window::event::RequestRedraw.doc: An event that indicates all of the application's windows should be redrawn, even if their control flow is set to `Wait` and there have been no window events.

bevy_window::event::WindowBackendScaleFa.doc: An event that indicates a window's OS-reported scale factor has changed.

fields.window: Window that had its scale factor changed by the backend.

bevy_window::event::WindowCloseRequested.doc: An event that is sent whenever the operating systems requests that a window be closed. This will be sent when the close button of the window is pressed.

bevy_window::event::WindowCreated.doc: An event that is sent whenever a new window is created.

bevy_window::event::WindowDestroyed.doc: An event that is sent whenever a window is destroyed by the underlying window system.

bevy_window::event::WindowEvent.doc: Wraps all `bevy_window` and `bevy_input` events in a common enum.

fields.CursorEntered: The user's cursor has entered a window.
fields.CursorLeft: The user's cursor has left a window.
fields.CursorMoved: The user's cursor has moved inside a window.
fields.FileDragAndDrop: A file drag and drop event.
fields.RequestRedraw: A redraw of all of the application's windows has been requested.
fields.WindowBackendScaleFactorChanged: The window's OS-reported scale factor has changed.
fields.WindowCloseRequested: The OS has requested that a window be closed.
fields.WindowCreated: A new window has been created.
fields.WindowDestroyed: A window has been destroyed by the underlying windowing system.
fields.WindowFocused: A window has received or lost focus.
fields.WindowOccluded: A window has started or stopped being occluded.
fields.WindowResized: A window's logical size has changed.
fields.WindowScaleFactorChanged: A window's scale factor has changed.
fields.WindowThemeChanged: Sent for windows that are using the system theme when the system theme changes.
fields.MouseButtonInput: The state of a mouse button has changed.
fields.MouseMotion: The physical position of a pointing device has changed.
fields.KeyboardFocusLost: Sent when focus has been lost for all Bevy windows.

bevy_window::event::WindowFocused.doc: An event that indicates a window has received or lost focus.

fields.focused: Whether it was focused (true) or lost focused (false).

bevy_window::event::WindowMoved.doc: An event that is sent when a window is repositioned in physical pixels.

fields.position: Where the window moved to in physical pixels.

bevy_window::event::WindowOccluded.doc: The window has been occluded (completely hidden from view).

fields.occluded: Whether it was occluded (true) or not occluded (false).

bevy_window::event::WindowResized.doc: A window event that is sent whenever a window's logical size has changed.

fields.width: The new logical width of the window.
fields.height: The new logical height of the window.

bevy_window::event::WindowScaleFactorCha.doc: An event that indicates a window's scale factor has changed.

fields.window: Window that had its scale factor changed.

bevy_window::event::WindowThemeChanged.doc: An event sent when the system theme changes for a window.

fields.window: Window for which the system theme has changed.

bevy_window::monitor::Monitor.doc: Represents an available monitor as reported by the user's operating system, which can be used to query information about the display, such as its size, position, and video modes.

fields.name: The name of the monitor
fields.physical_height: The height of the monitor in physical pixels
fields.physical_width: The width of the monitor in physical pixels
fields.physical_position: The position of the monitor in physical pixels
fields.refresh_rate_millihertz: The refresh rate of the monitor in millihertz
fields.scale_factor: The scale factor of the monitor
fields.video_modes: The video modes that the monitor supports

bevy_window::monitor::PrimaryMonitor.doc: A marker component for the primary monitor

bevy_window::monitor::VideoMode.doc: Represents a video mode that a monitor supports

fields.physical_size: The resolution of the video mode
fields.bit_depth: The bit depth of the video mode

bevy_window::window::CompositeAlphaMode.doc: Specifies how the alpha channel of the textures should be handled during compositing, for a `Window`.

fields.Auto: Chooses either `Opaque` or `Inherit` automatically, depending on the `alpha_mode` that the current surface can support.
fields.Opaque: The alpha channel, if it exists, of the textures is ignored in the compositing process. Instead, the textures is treated as if it has a constant alpha of 1.0.
fields.PreMultiplied: The alpha channel, if it exists, of the textures is respected in the compositing process. The non-alpha channels of the textures are expected to already be multiplied by the alpha channel by the application.
fields.PostMultiplied: The alpha channel, if it exists, of the textures is respected in the compositing process. The non-alpha channels of the textures are not expected to already be multiplied by the alpha channel by the application; instead, the compositor will multiply the non-alpha channels of the texture by the alpha channel during compositing.
fields.Inherit: The alpha channel, if it exists, of the textures is unknown for processing during compositing. Instead, the application is responsible for setting the composite alpha blending mode using native WSI command. If not set, then a platform-specific default will be used.

bevy_window::window::CursorGrabMode.doc: Defines if and how the cursor is grabbed by a `Window`.

fields.None: The cursor can freely leave the window.
fields.Confined: The cursor is confined to the window area.
fields.Locked: The cursor is locked inside the window area to a certain position.

fields.visible: Whether the cursor is visible or not.
fields.grab_mode: Whether or not the cursor is locked by or confined within the window.
fields.hit_test: Set whether or not mouse events within *this* window are captured or fall through to the Window below.

bevy_window::window::EnabledButtons.doc: Specifies which `Window` control buttons should be enabled.

fields.minimize: Enables the functionality of the minimize button.
fields.maximize: Enables the functionality of the maximize button.
fields.close: Enables the functionality of the close button.

bevy_window::window::InternalWindowState.doc: Stores internal `Window` state that isn't directly accessible.

fields.Current: Uses the current monitor of the window.
fields.Primary: Uses the primary monitor of the system.
fields.Index: Uses the monitor with the specified index.

bevy_window::window::NormalizedWindowRef.doc: A flattened representation of a window reference for equality/hashing purposes.

fields.Fifo: Presentation frames are kept in a First-In-First-Out queue approximately 3 frames long. Every vertical blanking period, the presentation engine will pop a frame off the queue to display. If there is no frame to display, it will present the same frame again until the next vblank.
fields.FifoRelaxed: Presentation frames are kept in a First-In-First-Out queue approximately 3 frames long. Every vertical blanking period, the presentation engine will pop a frame off the queue to display. If there is no frame to display, it will present the same frame until there is a frame in the queue. The moment there is a frame in the queue, it will immediately pop the frame off the queue.
fields.Immediate: Presentation frames are not queued at all. The moment a present command is executed on the GPU, the presented image is swapped onto the front buffer immediately.
fields.Mailbox: Presentation frames are kept in a single-frame queue. Every vertical blanking period, the presentation engine will pop a frame from the queue. If there is no frame to display, it will present the same frame again until the next vblank.

bevy_window::window::PrimaryWindow.doc: Marker `Component` for the window considered the primary window.

bevy_window::window::ScreenEdge.doc: The edges of a screen. Corresponds to `winit::platform::ios::ScreenEdge`.

fields.Top: The top edge of the screen.
fields.Left: The left edge of the screen.
fields.Bottom: The bottom edge of the screen.
fields.Right: The right edge of the screen.

bevy_window::window::VideoModeSelection.doc: References an exclusive fullscreen video mode.

fields.Current: Uses the video mode that the monitor is already in.
fields.Specific: Uses a given `VideoMode`. A list of video modes supported by the monitor is supplied by `Monitor::video_modes`.

bevy_window::window::Window.doc: The defining `Component` for window entities, storing information about how it should appear and behave.

fields.present_mode: What presentation mode to give the window.
fields.mode: Which fullscreen or windowing mode should be used.
fields.position: Where the window should be placed.
fields.resolution: What resolution the window should have.
fields.title: Stores the title of the window.
fields.name: Stores the application ID (on **`Wayland`**), `WM_CLASS` (on **`X11`**) or window class name (on **`Windows`**) of the window.
fields.composite_alpha_mode: How the alpha channel of textures should be handled while compositing.
fields.resize_constraints: The limits of the window's logical size (found in its `resolution`) when resizing.
fields.enabled_buttons: Specifies which window control buttons should be enabled.
fields.decorations: Should the window have decorations enabled?
fields.focused: Get/set whether the window is focused.
fields.window_level: Where should the window appear relative to other overlapping window.
fields.fit_canvas_to_parent: Whether or not to fit the canvas element's size to its parent element's size.
fields.prevent_default_event_handling: Whether or not to stop events from propagating out of the canvas element
fields.internal: Stores internal state that isn't directly accessible.
fields.ime_enabled: Should the window use Input Method Editor?
fields.ime_position: Sets location of IME candidate box in client area coordinates relative to the top left.
fields.window_theme: Sets a specific theme for the window.
fields.skip_taskbar: Sets whether the window should be shown in the taskbar.
fields.clip_children: Sets whether the window should draw over its child windows.
fields.desired_maximum_frame_latency: Optional hint given to the rendering API regarding the maximum number of queued frames admissible on the GPU.
fields.recognize_pan_gesture: Sets whether this window recognizes `PanGesture`, with a number of fingers between the first value and the last.
fields.movable_by_window_background: Enables click-and-drag behavior for the entire window, not just the titlebar.
fields.fullsize_content_view: Makes the window content appear behind the titlebar.
fields.has_shadow: Toggles drawing the drop shadow behind the window.
fields.titlebar_transparent: Makes the titlebar transparent, allowing the app content to appear behind it.
fields.titlebar_show_buttons: Toggles showing the traffic light window buttons.
fields.borderless_game: Hides the dock and menu bar when a borderless fullscreen window is active.
fields.prefers_home_indicator_hidden: Sets whether the Window prefers the home indicator hidden.
fields.prefers_status_bar_hidden: Sets whether the Window prefers the status bar hidden.
fields.preferred_screen_edges_deferring_system_: Sets screen edges for which you want your gestures to take precedence over the system gestures.

bevy_window::window::WindowLevel.doc: Specifies where a `Window` should appear relative to other overlapping windows (on top or under) .

fields.AlwaysOnBottom: The window will always be below `WindowLevel::Normal` and `WindowLevel::AlwaysOnTop` windows.
fields.AlwaysOnTop: The window will always be on top of `WindowLevel::Normal` and `WindowLevel::AlwaysOnBottom` windows.

bevy_window::window::WindowMode.doc: Defines the way a `Window` is displayed.

fields.Windowed: The window should take a portion of the screen, using the window resolution size.
fields.BorderlessFullscreen: The window should appear fullscreen by being borderless and using the full size of the screen on the given `MonitorSelection`.
fields.Fullscreen: The window should be in "true"/"legacy"/"exclusive" Fullscreen mode on the given `MonitorSelection`.

bevy_window::window::WindowPosition.doc: Defines where a `Window` should be placed on the screen.

fields.Automatic: Position will be set by the window manager. Bevy will delegate this decision to the window manager and no guarantees can be made about where the window will be placed.
fields.Centered: Window will be centered on the selected monitor.
fields.At: The window's top-left corner should be placed at the specified position (in physical pixels).

bevy_window::window::WindowRef.doc: Reference to a `Window`, whether it be a direct link to a specific entity or a more vague defaulting choice.

fields.Primary: This will be linked to the primary window that is created by default in the `WindowPlugin`.
fields.Entity: A more direct link to a window entity.

fields.min_width: The minimum width the window can have.
fields.min_height: The minimum height the window can have.
fields.max_width: The maximum width the window can have.
fields.max_height: The maximum height the window can have.

bevy_world_serialization::components::Dy.doc: Adding this component will spawn the world as a child of that entity. Once it's spawned, the entity will have a `WorldInstance` component.

bevy_world_serialization::components::Wo.doc: Adding this component will spawn the world as a child of that entity. Once it's spawned, the entity will have a `WorldInstance` component.

fields.Once: once, and it stays at the end
fields.Loop: from the start again each time

raea_bevy_adapters::easings::EaseSpriteC.doc: Eases the entity's Sprite colour to `to` over `seconds`, from its colour when this is added or changed.

raea_bevy_adapters::easings::EaseTransfo.doc: Eases the entity's Transform to `to` over `seconds`, from where it is when this is added or changed.

fields.function: Bevy's easing curves: "Linear" and the ones bevy_easings has too ("QuadraticInOut", "BounceOut", ...; see method)
fields.repeat: Bevy's easing curves: "Linear" and the ones bevy_easings has too ("QuadraticInOut", "BounceOut", ...; see method)

raea_bevy_adapters::enoki::Sparks.doc: A stream of particles from the entity it's on, built into an enoki spawner and effect when added.

fields.direction: the way they leave (+y up the frame)
fields.spread: how far from `direction` they spread (0 none, 1 all the way round; above 0 differs from run to run)
fields.gravity: downward pull, pixels a second each second

raea_bevy_adapters::ldtk::CurrentLevel.doc: The level to show, by its index in the project (0 the first); put it on the LdtkProjectHandle's entity.

raea_bevy_adapters::light_2d::Lighting2d.doc: The 2D overlay's ambient light, from any entity it's on.

raea_bevy_adapters::rapier2d::ColliderSh.doc: A 2D collider's shape, built into rapier's Collider on the entity it's on (metres, +y up).

fields.Cuboid: half of its size on each axis
fields.Capsule: along y: half the straight part's height, and the radius of its ends

raea_bevy_adapters::rapier3d::ColliderSh.doc: A 2D collider's shape, built into rapier's Collider on the entity it's on (metres, +y up).

fields.Cuboid: half of its size on each axis
fields.Capsule: along y: half the straight part's height, and the radius of its ends

raea_bevy_adapters::spritesheet::SheetAn.doc: A sprite playing cells of a sheet in a loop, built into a Sprite and a SpritesheetAnimation when added.

fields.image_size: the image's size in pixels (the atlas is laid out before the image loads)
fields.columns: the image's size in pixels (the atlas is laid out before the image loads)
fields.rows: the image's size in pixels (the atlas is laid out before the image loads)
fields.frames: the cells played, numbered row by row from the top left
fields.size: its size on the frame in pixels

raea_bevy_adapters::text3d::Label3d.doc: One line of text drawn as a mesh in the 3D scene, built into bevy_rich_text3d's parts when added.

fields.world_scale: the em's height in metres (bevy_rich_text3d's world_scale, as raea's own text sets it)
fields.font: a loaded font's family ("Fira Mono", the one always loaded)

raea_bevy_calls::sprite3d::SpriteQuad.doc: A sprite on a quad: Bevy's Sprite and bevy_sprite3d's Sprite3d from one reflected component

fields.image: the image, as the bridge reads any Handle<Image>: a path (beside the composition, or in media), an inline {width, height, pixels} picture, or "render:NAME"
fields.pixels_per_metre: the image, as the bridge reads any Handle<Image>: a path (beside the composition, or in media), an inline {width, height, pixels} picture, or "render:NAME"
fields.pivot: None centres it; (0, 0) to (1, 1) across the sprite
fields.unlit: None centres it; (0, 0) to (1, 1) across the sprite
fields.double_sided: None centres it; (0, 0) to (1, 1) across the sprite
fields.blend: alpha blended, where the default cuts out at 0.5
fields.emissive: alpha blended, where the default cuts out at 0.5
fields.atlas: a cell of a sprite sheet, when the image is one

raea_bevy_calls::sprite3d::SpriteSheet.doc: A grid of equal cells, numbered row by row from the top left

raea_bevy_plugins::enhanced_input::OnFoo.doc: The on-foot input context: a game's player carries it.

raea_bevy_plugins::hanabi::Particles.doc: A fountain of particles from the entity it's on (a Mesh), built into a hanabi effect (on a child of it) when added.

fields.spread: how far from straight up they spread (0 straight, 1 a hemisphere)
fields.opaque: alpha-blended (soft, drawn in an order the GPU chooses) or opaque

raea_bevy_plugins::lightyear::Announce.doc: A line for the peer's log, read by a system the next frame (a reflected message: world.write_message).

raea_bevy_plugins::lightyear::Announced.doc: The lines Announce has written, in order (a reflected resource: world.get_resources).

raea_bevy_plugins::lightyear::Position.doc: Where a networked thing is: replicated from the server, predicted on its controlling client.

raea_bevy_plugins::lightyear::Session.doc: Where the session is: input moves the player only while Playing (a reflected, freely mutable state, so TypeScript reads and sets it through raea/state.get and raea/state.set).

raea_bevy_plugins::lightyear::Teleport.doc: Moves every networked thing on the peer it's triggered on to `to` (a reflected event: world.trigger_event, and world.observe+watch sees it).

raea_bevy_plugins::tnua::TnuaInput.doc: What the character is asked to do this step, set from TypeScript.

raea_core_animate::spec::AnimKey.doc: One key: a value at a local frame, and the curve from it to the next key.

fields.color: a colour property's value (CSS text); empty for numbers
fields.ease: the curve to the next key (easing::Easing::parse); empty is linear

fields.prop: the property it keys: opacity, x, y, z, scale, rotate, width, height, blur, clip, a colour, `text`, or another number
fields.repeat: past the last key: "" or "hold", "loop", "pingpong" (for ever), or "loop:N" / "pingpong:N"
fields.digits: decimals a `text` number is written with
fields.prefix: written before and after a `text` number (a counter's "$" and " pts")
fields.separator: between a `text` number's thousands ("," writes 12,345); empty: none

fields.origin: the composition frame the element's local frame 0 falls on (where its Sequence starts)
fields.freeze: a local frame to hold at whatever the composition's frame (inside a Freeze)
fields.fps: the frames per second its frames count; springs measure their settle time with it (0: the clock's)
fields.tracks: the element's keyframed properties, one track each
fields.show_from: the local frame it's shown from, when it shows only for a window (mount="during"); before it, display none
fields.show_until: the local frame it's hidden from again

raea_sys_compute::Computes.doc: The frame's computes, in order, and the frame's time.

raea_sys_phase::DepthCopy.doc: The image a camera's depth is copied into each frame.

raea_sys_phase::GBufferPass.doc: A camera's fullscreen G-buffer draw: its shader file (as written), its G-buffer entry point and its shadow one ("" for none).

fields.registered: its shader file, registered as written (raea-sys-shader), and the id register gave it

raea_sys_phase::MeshPass.doc: A mesh's own pass: its shader file (as written) and entry points.

fields.depth: whether it tests and writes the view's depth (GreaterEqual), as a mesh in Bevy's opaque phase does
fields.registered: its shader file, registered as written (raea-sys-shader), and the id register gave it

raea_sys_phase::MeshShaderPass.doc: A camera's mesh-shader draw: its task shader file ("" for none), mesh and fragment shader files, and its workgroup count.

fields.registered: its files, registered as written (raea-sys-shader), and the ids register gave them (0 for no task shader)

raea_sys_phase::PhaseItem.doc: What a phase item draws: its shader file (as written) and entry points, its vertex buffer's words (32-bit each, each `stride` bytes a vertex) and attributes, its indices (u32), and its depth state: whether it writes depth and how it compares (Bevy's CompareFunction by name).

fields.registered: its shader file, registered as written (raea-sys-shader), and the id register gave it

raea_sys_phase::ShaderInstances.doc: A mesh's instances: your shader file (as written), and each instance's `stride` bytes of 32-bit words, read as its `attributes` say.

fields.registered: its shader file, registered as written (raea-sys-shader), and the id register gave it

name:Annulus.doc: A primitive shape formed by the region between two circles, also known as a ring.

fields.inner_circle: The inner circle of the annulus
fields.outer_circle: The outer circle of the annulus

name:Atmosphere.doc: Atmosphere for one planet. The entity's `GlobalTransform` is the planet center in world space.

fields.outer_radius: Radius at which we consider the atmosphere to 'end' for our calculations (from center of planet)
fields.ground_albedo: An approximation of the average albedo (or color, roughly) of the planet's surface. This is used when calculating multiscattering.
fields.medium: A handle to a `ScatteringMedium`, which describes the substance of the atmosphere and how it scatters light.

name:Capsule2d.doc: A 2D capsule primitive, also known as a stadium or pill shape.

fields.half_length: Half the height of the capsule, excluding the semicircles

name:Capsule3d.doc: A 3D capsule primitive centered on the origin A three-dimensional capsule is defined as a surface at a distance (radius) from a line

fields.half_length: Half the height of the capsule, excluding the hemispheres

name:Circle.doc: A circle primitive, representing the set of points some distance from the origin

name:CircularSector.doc: A primitive representing a circular sector: a pie slice of a circle.

name:CircularSegment.doc: A primitive representing a circular segment: the area enclosed by the arc of a circle and its chord (the line between its endpoints).

name:Cone.doc: A cone primitive centered on the midpoint between the tip of the cone and the center of its base.

name:ConicalFrustum.doc: A conical frustum primitive. A conical frustum can be created by slicing off a section of a cone.

fields.radius_top: The radius of the top of the frustum
fields.radius_bottom: The radius of the base of the frustum

name:Cylinder.doc: A cylinder primitive centered on the origin

fields.half_height: The half height of the cylinder

name:Ellipse.doc: An ellipse primitive, which is like a circle, but the width and height can be different

fields.half_size: Half of the width and height of the ellipse.

name:ExtendedMaterial.doc: A material that extends a base `Material` with additional shaders and data.

name:LensDistortion.doc: Simulates the warping of the image caused by real-world camera lenses.

fields.intensity: The overall strength of the distortion effect.
fields.scale: A global scale factor applied to the final distorted image.
fields.multiplier: A multiplier that determines how the distortion scales along the X and Y axes.
fields.center: The center point of the distortion effect in UV space `[0.0, 1.0]`.
fields.edge_curvature: Controls the sharpness of the distortion curve near the screen edges.

name:Plane3d.doc: A bounded plane in 3D space. It forms a surface starting from the origin with a defined height and width.

fields.normal: The normal of the plane. The plane will be placed perpendicular to this direction
fields.half_size: Half of the width and height of the plane

name:Polyline2d.doc: A series of connected line segments in 2D space.

name:RegularPolygon.doc: A polygon centered on the origin where all vertices lie on a circle, equally far apart.

fields.circumcircle: The circumcircle on which all vertices lie

name:Rhombus.doc: A rhombus primitive, also known as a diamond shape. A four sided polygon, centered on the origin, where opposite sides are parallel but without requiring right angles.

fields.half_diagonals: Size of the horizontal and vertical diagonals of the rhombus

name:Segment2d.doc: A line segment defined by two endpoints in 2D space.

fields.vertices: The endpoints of the line segment.

name:TextureView.doc: Describes a `Texture` with its associated metadata required by a pipeline or `BindGroup`.

name:Torus.doc: A torus primitive, often representing a ring or donut shape The set of points some distance from a circle centered at the origin

fields.minor_radius: The radius of the tube of the torus
fields.major_radius: The distance from the center of the torus to the center of the tube
